# Council packet: bennett-conformance checker quality floor (checker verdicts = oracle; R32.3)

Repository: bennett-conformance. Base: main e39501e (local; origin lags). Candidate: a00ab18 (branch job/quality-checker).
Range main..a00ab18: earlier sol-checker / quality-checker round-1 work (eq2 strict §16.1 object lexical validation, inherited
890/gm5/37u/2hl/zlo/30g regressions, recompute-cleanup explicit `unchecked`), then the r2 resume: one pinned ISA 3b10907 for
tests, neutral suite and the interpreter (BENNETT_ISA_SPEC / BENNETT_ISA_BINARY via gate.toml [env]); K89 borrow_frame /
workspace / entry_products handled as explicit `unchecked` where not derived; test consolidation; replay phase split
(check_replay_inner etc.); fail-fast fixes; value mutations in the mutation sweep; clause tags; quality ratchet; hygiene. Code
review round 1 BLOCK (mge: non-canonical §16.1 width/bound spellings verified as proof) -> fixed in 07beada + a00ab18 with a
generated checker-vs-reference lexical differential (1,933 cases, 52 numeric + 183 punctuation sites, 0 disagreements). Code
review round 2 (last) runs alongside this council. Implementer: gpt-6.1-sol. Gate (full repo gate_run) on a00ab18 runs before
this round; 5aa394f (pre-fix) passed.

Implementer's verification (reproduce what you need): checker cargo test 291 pass, 29.75 s; coverage 84.19 % (lexical reader
97.10 %); clause tests 113, suite tests 23, neutral suite 16 cases. Open follow-ups (disclosed, not claimed): ac5 fv9 8v5 hql pem
bnk jvq cnf 5na (coverage, clause map, nine over-long functions, default audit, litter, full K89 derivation).

Rulings requested: (1) Does any verdict path report verified for something the checker does not actually check (incl. the K89
`unchecked` handling and the recompute-cleanup guard)? (2) Is the replay phase split behaviour-identical on verdicts? (3) Can the
generated lexical differential and the value-mutation sweep actually fail (both directions)?

+#[cfg(test)]
+mod fail_fast_tests {

+    #[test]
+    fn lifted_calls_cannot_create_missing_target_or_fault_values_from_zero() {
+        let object = Object::parse(include_str!(

+        ))
+        .unwrap();
+        for missing in ["t", "fr"] {
+            let mut work = 100;
+            let mut env = Lifted {
+                object: &object,
+                vals: HashMap::from([
+                    ("x".into(), 7u32.into()),
+                    ("t".into(), 0u32.into()),
+                    ("fr".into(), 0u32.into()),
+                ]),
+                widths: HashMap::from([("x".into(), 4), ("t".into(), 4), ("fr".into(), 4)]),
+                tokens: HashMap::from([(
+                    "tk".into(),
+                    [9u32.into(), 4u32.into(), 0u32.into(), 0u32.into()],
+                )]),
+                result_val: 0u32.into(),
+                tgt_width: 4,
+                depth: 0,
+                work: &mut work,
+                oracle_name: "o".into(),
+                heap_limit: 4u32.into(),
+                memory: None,
+                locations: HashSet::from(["t".into(), "fr".into()]),
+                fault_width: 4,
+                region_names: HashMap::new(),
+                in_lproc: false,
+            };
+            env.vals.remove(missing);
+            let toks =
+                ["lift.oracle_call", "@o", "tk", "(x)", "t", "fr", "()", "()"].map(str::to_string);
+            match env.exec_row(&toks, &[], &HashMap::new(), &mut HashMap::new(), &[]) {
+                Err(EvalError::Reject(error)) => {
+                    assert_eq!(error.code, "E_CERT_OBJECT");
+                    assert!(error.message.contains(missing), "{error:?}");
+                }
+                _ => panic!("missing {missing} was silently initialized by the call"),
+            }
+        }
+    }
+}
diff --git a/checker/src/eval/borrow_frames.rs b/checker/src/eval/borrow_frames.rs
new file mode 100644
index 0000000..ed156f9
--- /dev/null
+++ b/checker/src/eval/borrow_frames.rs
@@ -0,0 +1,101 @@
+//! Selected §12.1/§12.2 borrow frames. Schema admission grants no proof:
+//! normative entry domains, occurrence identities and tensor factors remain
+//! obligations until they can be derived independently.
+use super::*;
+use crate::cert::{check_keys, Subject};
+
+#[allow(clippy::too_many_arguments)]
+pub(super) fn check_claim(
+    claim: &Value,
+    path: &str,
+    subject: &Subject,
+    symbol: &Symbol,
+    iface: &Interface,
+    docs: &LoadedDocs,
+    root_invocation: &Option<Invocation>,
+    cert_schedule_hash: Option<&str>,
+) -> Result<ClaimOutcome, ClaimOutcome> {
+    let mut errors = vec![];
+    let frame = claim.get("borrow_frame").unwrap_or(&Value::Null);
+    check_keys(
+        frame,
+        &["lifetime", "first", "last", "context_key"],
+        &["lifetime", "first", "last"],
+        &format!("{path}.borrow_frame"),
+        &mut errors,
+    );
+    if let Some(lifetime) = frame.get("lifetime") {
+        crate::domain::biguint_of_json(lifetime, "borrow_frame.lifetime").map_err(|e| match e {
+            ResolveError::Reject(r) => ClaimOutcome::rejected(vec![r.at(path)]),
+            ResolveError::HostLimit(h) => host_limit_outcome(h),
+        })?;
+    }
+    let scheduled = subject.schedule_hash.is_some();
+    if scheduled && subject.schedule_hash.as_deref() != cert_schedule_hash {
+        errors.push(rej(
+            "E_CERT_BINDING",
+            "§12.3",
+            path,
+            "borrow-frame subject schedule does not match certificate binding",
+        ));
+    }
+    if scheduled {
+        match frame.get("context_key").and_then(Value::as_arr) {
+            None => errors.push(schema_err(
+                format!("{path}.borrow_frame.context_key"),
+                "schedule-bound borrow frame requires a resolved invocation key",
+            )),
+            Some(key) if subject.closure_hash == docs.root_closure && !key.is_empty() => errors
+                .push(rej(
+                    "E_CERT_BINDING",
+                    "§12.1",
+                    path,
+                    "root borrow-frame context_key must be []",
+                )),
+            Some(_) => (),
+        }
+    }
+    match claim.get("invocation") {
+        Some(v) => {
+            let inv = parse_invocation_for_kind(
+                v,
+                &iface.args,
+                &docs.object,
+                &symbol.kind,
+                &format!("{path}.invocation"),
+            )
+            .map_err(ClaimOutcome::rejected)?;
+            if scheduled && subject.closure_hash == docs.root_closure {
+                if let Some(root) = root_invocation {
+                    if inv.args != root.args
+                        || inv.budget != root.budget
+                        || inv.token_aliases != root.token_aliases
+                    {
+                        errors.push(rej(
+                            "E_CERT_BINDING",
+                            "§12.3",
+                            path,
+                            "borrow-frame invocation conflicts with root binding",
+                        ));
+                    }
+                }
+            }
+        }
+        None if !scheduled => errors.push(rej(
+            "E_CERT_INVOCATION",
+            "§12.3",
+            path,
+            "standalone borrow-frame claim requires explicit invocation",
+        )),
+        None => (),
+    }
+    if !errors.is_empty() {
+        return Err(ClaimOutcome::rejected(errors));
+    }
+    // Do not run an ordinary interface-domain proof on a selected frame.
+    // In particular, workspace and entry_products describe frame-entry
+    // states, which resolve_domain intentionally cannot certify.
+    Ok(ClaimOutcome::unchecked(
+        "selected borrow-frame occurrence resolution, normative entry domain (workspace/entry_products), sampler and tensor-factor replay have not been independently derived (§12.1/§12.2)",
+    ))
+}
diff --git a/checker/src/eval/replay_claim.rs b/checker/src/eval/replay_claim.rs
new file mode 100644
index 0000000..a620fe4
--- /dev/null
+++ b/checker/src/eval/replay_claim.rs
@@ -0,0 +1,508 @@
+//! Named schema, relation, table, program and enumeration phases for §12 replay.
+use super::*;
+
+pub(super) fn validate_shape(claim: &Value, kind: &str, path: &str) -> Result<(), ClaimOutcome> {
+    let mut errs = Vec::new();
+    let allowed: &[&str] = if kind == "sampled" {
+        &[
+            "kind",
+            "subject",
+            "domain",
+            "expected",
+            "sampler",
+            "label",
+            "invocation",
+        ]
+    } else {
+        &[
+            "kind",
+            "subject",
+            "domain",
+            "expected",
+            "label",
+            "invocation",
+        ]
+    };
+    let mut allowed = allowed.to_vec();
+    if claim.get("expected").and_then(Value::as_str) == Some("borrow_frame") {
+        allowed.push("borrow_frame");
+    }
+    let required: &[&str] = if kind == "sampled" {
+        &["kind", "subject", "domain", "expected", "sampler"]
+    } else {
+        &["kind", "subject", "domain", "expected"]
+    };
+    if let Some(obj) = claim.as_obj() {
+        for k in obj.keys() {
+            if !allowed.contains(&k.as_str()) {
+                errs.push(schema_err(
+                    format!("{path}.{k}"),
+                    format!("unknown field {k:?} in {kind} claim"),
+                ));
+            }
+        }
+        for r in required {
+            if !obj.contains_key(*r) {
+                errs.push(schema_err(
+                    format!("{path}.{r}"),
+                    format!("missing required field {r:?}"),
+                ));
+            }
+        }
+    } else {
+        errs.push(schema_err(path.to_string(), "claim is not an object"));
+    }
+    if !errs.is_empty() {
+        return Err(ClaimOutcome::rejected(errs));
+    }
+    Ok(())
+}
+
+#[derive(PartialEq)]
+pub(super) enum Expected {
+    Oracle,
+    InversePair,
+    BorrowFrame,
+    Table(Vec<Value>),
+    Program(String),
+}
+
+pub(super) fn parse_expected(claim: &Value, path: &str) -> Result<Expected, ClaimOutcome> {
+    Ok(match claim.get("expected") {
+        Some(Value::Str(x)) if x == "oracle" => Expected::Oracle,
+        Some(Value::Str(x)) if x == "inverse_pair" => Expected::InversePair,
+        Some(Value::Str(x)) if x == "borrow_frame" => Expected::BorrowFrame,
+        Some(Value::Obj(m)) if m.len() == 1 && m.contains_key("table") => {
+            match m.get("table").and_then(Value::as_arr) {
+                Some(rows) => Expected::Table(rows.to_vec()),
+                None => return Err(ClaimOutcome::rejected(vec![rej("E_CERT_TABLE", "§12.1", format!("{path}.expected.table"), "expected array of before/after rows")])),
+            }
+        }
+        Some(Value::Obj(m)) if m.len() == 1 && m.contains_key("program") => {
+            match m.get("program").and_then(Value::as_str).filter(|h| crate::is_hash_hex(h)) {
+                Some(h) => Expected::Program(h.to_string()),
+                None => {
+                    return Err(ClaimOutcome::rejected(vec![schema_err(
+                        format!("{path}.expected.program"),
+                        "expected closure hash",
+                    )]))
+                }
+            }
+        }
+        _ => {
+            return Err(ClaimOutcome::rejected(vec![rej(
+                "E_CERT_BINDING",
+                "§12.1",
+                format!("{path}.expected"),
+                "expected must be \"borrow_frame\", \"oracle\", {table}, {program}, or (exhaustive) \"inverse_pair\"; there is no default relation",
+            )]))
+        }
+    })
+}
+
+pub(super) fn table_rows(
+    expected: &Expected,
+    domain: &ResolvedDomain,
+    path: &str,
+) -> Result<Option<Vec<(Tuple, Tuple)>>, ClaimOutcome> {
+    Ok(match &expected {
+        Expected::Table(rows) => {
+            if BigUint::from(rows.len()) != domain.n {
+                return Err(ClaimOutcome::rejected(vec![rej(
+                    "E_CERT_TABLE",
+                    "§12.1",
+                    format!("{path}.expected.table"),
+                    format!(
+                        "table has {} rows; the declared domain has {} elements",
+                        rows.len(),
+                        domain.n
+                    ),
+                )]));
+            }
+            // Both before/after tuples are retained. Validate the entire
+            // declared table even when only a drawn subset will execute.
+            if let Err(limit) = domain.check_retained_elements(&(BigUint::from(rows.len()) * 2u32))
+            {
+                return Err(host_limit_outcome(limit));
+            }
+            let mut parsed = Vec::new();
+            for (i, (row, element)) in rows.iter().zip(domain.elements()).enumerate() {
+                let mut errors = vec![];
+                if !crate::cert::check_keys(
+                    row,
+                    &["before", "after"],
+                    &["before", "after"],
+                    &format!("{path}.expected.table[{i}]"),
+                    &mut errors,
+                ) {
+                    for error in &mut errors {
+                        error.code = "E_CERT_TABLE";
+                    }
+                    return Err(ClaimOutcome::rejected(errors));
+                }
+                let before = parse_tuple(
+                    row.get("before").unwrap_or(&Value::Null),
+                    &domain,
+                    &format!("{path}.expected.table[{i}].before"),
+                )
+                .map_err(|e| ClaimOutcome::rejected(vec![e]))?;
+                if before != element {
+                    return Err(ClaimOutcome::rejected(vec![rej(
+                        "E_CERT_TABLE",
+                        "§12.1",
+                        format!("{path}.expected.table[{i}].before"),
+                        format!(
+                            "row before {} is not declared-domain element {i} {}",
+                            fmt_tuple(&before),
+                            fmt_tuple(&element)
+                        ),
+                    )]));
+                }
+                let after = parse_tuple(
+                    row.get("after").unwrap_or(&Value::Null),
+                    &domain,
+                    &format!("{path}.expected.table[{i}].after"),
+                )
+                .map_err(|e| ClaimOutcome::rejected(vec![e]))?;
+                parsed.push((before, after));
+            }
+            Some(parsed)
+        }
+        _ => None,
+    })
+}
+
+pub(super) fn bind_program(
+    expected: &Expected,
+    iface: &Interface,
+    docs: &LoadedDocs,
+    path: &str,
+) -> Result<Option<(Symbol, Interface)>, ClaimOutcome> {
+    Ok(match &expected {
+        Expected::Program(h) => {
+            let sym = match docs.object.symbol_by_closure(h) {
+                Some(s) => s.clone(),
+                None if docs.object.imports.is_empty() => return Err(ClaimOutcome::rejected(vec![rej(
+                    "E_CERT_BINDING", "§12.1", format!("{path}.expected.program"),
+                    "expected program closure is absent from the complete supplied object (no imports)",
+                )])),
+                None => {
+                    return Err(ClaimOutcome::unchecked(
+                        "expected program is not in the supplied object",
+                    ))
+                }
+            };
+            let piface = docs
+                .object
+                .interface(&sym.name)
+                .map_err(|e| ClaimOutcome::unchecked(format!("expected program interface: {e}")))?;
+            let shape = |i: &Interface| {
+                (
+                    i.bundles
+                        .iter()
+                        .map(|b| (b.group.clone(), b.width))
+                        .collect::<Vec<_>>(),
+                    i.regions
+                        .iter()
+                        .map(|r| (r.role.clone(), r.a, r.w))
+                        .collect::<Vec<_>>(),
+                    i.args.clone(),
+                    i.borrowed_widths.clone(),
+                )
+            };
+            if shape(&iface) != shape(&piface) {
+                return Err(ClaimOutcome::rejected(vec![rej(
+                    "E_CERT_BINDING",
+                    "§12.1",
+                    format!("{path}.expected.program"),
+                    "expected program signature is not compatible with the subject (roles, widths, region shapes, argument types, borrowed widths)",
+                )]));
+            }
+            Some((sym, piface))
+        }
+        _ => None,
+    })
+}
+
+pub(super) fn select_elements(
+    claim: &Value,
+    kind: &str,
+    domain: &ResolvedDomain,
+    inputs: &Inputs,
+    path: &str,
+) -> Result<(Vec<Tuple>, Option<u64>, Option<usize>), ClaimOutcome> {
+    Ok(if kind == "exhaustive" {
+        if domain.n > BigUint::from(inputs.limits.max_elements) {
+            return Err(host_limit_outcome(crate::fault::HostLimit {
+                quantity: format!(
+                    "domain element count {} (cap {})",
+                    domain.n, inputs.limits.max_elements
+                ),
+            }));
+        }
+        if let Err(h) = domain.check_retained_elements(&domain.n) {
+            return Err(host_limit_outcome(h));
+        }
+        (domain.elements().collect(), None, None)
+    } else {
+        let sampler = claim.get("sampler").cloned().unwrap_or(Value::Null);
+        let mut errs = Vec::new();
+        crate::cert::check_keys(
+            &sampler,
+            &["algorithm", "seed", "count"],
+            &["algorithm", "seed", "count"],
+            &format!("{path}.sampler"),
+            &mut errs,
+        );
+        if sampler.get("algorithm").and_then(Value::as_str) != Some("xoshiro256**") {
+            errs.push(rej(
+                "E_CERT_SAMPLER",
+                "§12.1",
+                format!("{path}.sampler.algorithm"),
+                "algorithm must be \"xoshiro256**\"",
+            ));
+        }
+        let seed: Vec<String> = sampler
+            .get("seed")
+            .and_then(Value::as_arr)
+            .map(|a| {
+                a.iter()
+                    .filter_map(|x| x.as_str().map(str::to_string))
+                    .collect()
+            })
+            .unwrap_or_default();
+        if seed.len() != 4
+            || sampler.get("seed").and_then(Value::as_arr).map(|a| a.len()) != Some(4)
+        {
+            errs.push(rej(
+                "E_CERT_SAMPLER",
+                "§12.1",
+                format!("{path}.sampler.seed"),
+                "seed must be 4 decimal strings",
+            ));
+        }
+        let count = sampler
+            .get("count")
+            .and_then(|v| {
+                v.as_str()
+                    .and_then(crate::rat::parse_biguint_str)
+                    .or_else(|| u64_of(v).map(BigUint::from))
+            })
+            .unwrap_or_else(|| {
+                errs.push(rej(
+                    "E_CERT_SAMPLER",
+                    "§12.1",
+                    format!("{path}.sampler.count"),
+                    "count must be a nonnegative integer",
+                ));
+                BigUint::zero()
+            });
+        if !errs.is_empty() {
+            return Err(ClaimOutcome::rejected(errs));
+        }
+        if let Err(e) = crate::sampler::Sampler::new([&seed[0], &seed[1], &seed[2], &seed[3]]) {
+            return Err(ClaimOutcome::rejected(vec![rej(
+                "E_CERT_SAMPLER",
+                "§12.1",
+                format!("{path}.sampler.seed"),
+                e,
+            )]));
+        }
+        if count > BigUint::from(inputs.limits.max_elements) {
+            return Err(host_limit_outcome(crate::fault::HostLimit {
+                quantity: format!("sampler count {count} (cap {})", inputs.limits.max_elements),
+            }));
+        }
+        if let Err(h) = domain.check_retained_elements(&count) {
+            return Err(host_limit_outcome(h));
+        }
+        let count = count
+            .to_string()
+            .parse::<u64>()
+            .expect("count was bounded by the u64 host limit");
+        let draws = match crate::sampler::draw_elements(
+            &domain,
+            [&seed[0], &seed[1], &seed[2], &seed[3]],
+            count,
+        ) {
+            Ok(d) => d,
+            Err(ResolveError::Reject(r)) => return Err(ClaimOutcome::rejected(vec![r.at(path)])),
+            Err(ResolveError::HostLimit(h)) => return Err(host_limit_outcome(h)),
+        };
+        let distinct: std::collections::HashSet<String> = draws.iter().map(fmt_tuple).collect();
+        (draws, Some(count), Some(distinct.len()))
+    })
+}
+
+#[allow(clippy::too_many_arguments)]
+pub(super) fn finish_outcome(
+    kind: &str,
+    domain: &ResolvedDomain,
+    invocation: &Invocation,
+    subject: &crate::cert::Subject,
+    scheduled: bool,
+    requested_label: Option<String>,
+    draws_count: Option<u64>,
+    distinct_count: Option<usize>,
+    path: &str,
+) -> Result<ClaimOutcome, ClaimOutcome> {
+    let (computed, elements_s, fraction) = if kind == "exhaustive" {
+        (
+            if domain.covers_full {
+                "proof"
+            } else if domain.covers_relative_to_image {
+                "proof_relative_to_image"
+            } else {
+                "evidence"
+            },
+            domain.n.to_string(),
+            domain.covered_fraction(),
+        )
+    } else {
+        (
+            "evidence",
+            draws_count
+                .expect("sampled replay records a draw count")
+                .to_string(),
+            fraction_string(
+                &BigUint::from(distinct_count.expect("sampled replay records a distinct count")),
+                &domain.full_n,
+            ),
+        )
+    };
+    let mut out = ClaimOutcome {
+        outcome: computed.into(),
+        establishes: String::new(),
+        elements: Some(elements_s.clone()),
+        draws: draws_count.map(|d| d.to_string()),
+        distinct: distinct_count.map(|d| d.to_string()),
+        covered_fraction: Some(fraction.clone()),
+        token_aliases: Some(invocation.token_aliases.clone()),
+        image_bindings: if domain.fixed_regions.is_empty() {
+            None
+        } else {
+            let regions = domain
+                .fixed_regions
+                .iter()
+                .map(|r| {
+                    Value::Obj(std::collections::BTreeMap::from([
+                        (
+                            "identity".into(),
+                            Value::Arr(vec![Value::Str("mem".into()), crate::json::n(r.position)]),
+                        ),
+                        ("A".into(), crate::json::n(r.a)),
+                        ("W".into(), crate::json::n(r.w)),
+                        ("sha256".into(), Value::Str(r.sha256.clone())),
+                    ]))
+                })
+                .collect();
+            Some(Value::Obj(std::collections::BTreeMap::from([
+                ("fixed_regions".into(), Value::Arr(regions)),
+                ("context_key".into(), Value::Arr(vec![])),
+                (
+                    "invocation".into(),
+                    Value::Obj(std::collections::BTreeMap::from([
+                        ("args".into(), Value::Arr(invocation.args.clone())),
+                        (
+                            "budget".into(),
+                            Value::Arr(
+                                invocation
+                                    .budget
+                                    .iter()
+                                    .map(|n| Value::Str(n.to_string()))
+                                    .collect(),
+                            ),
+                        ),
+                        (
+                            "token_aliases".into(),
+                            Value::Arr(
+                                invocation
+                                    .token_aliases
+                                    .iter()
+                                    .map(crate::json::n)
+                                    .collect(),
+                            ),
+                        ),
+                    ])),
+                ),
+            ])))
+        },
+        ..Default::default()
+    };
+    out.establishes = if computed == "proof" {
+        format!(
+            "every element of D ({elements_s} tuples) was replayed and full output tuples agree with the expected relation under the subject {} variant {:?} with {} inherited control(s); by §12.2 this is proof (and the §14.3 T3 premise for permutation subjects)",
+            if scheduled { "realised (schedule-bound, exact) " } else { "" },
+            subject.variant,
+            subject.inherited_controls
+        )
+    } else if computed == "proof_relative_to_image" {
+        format!("all {elements_s} tuples of every remaining unrestricted component were replayed with the independently bound fixed image(s); this is a conditional proof_relative_to_image theorem with exact +1 phase, full outputs, input-image restoration and clean workspace, covering {fraction} of unrestricted D; executable preparation and entry factorisation are separate obligations, not established by this theorem")
+    } else if kind == "exhaustive" {
+        format!("all {elements_s} domain elements were replayed and agree; this is evidence over a strict slice of D (covered fraction {fraction}), never proof")
+    } else {
+        format!(
+            "{} sampled draws ({} distinct) were replayed on both sides and agree; sampled success is always evidence (distinct covered fraction {fraction}), even at full coverage",
+            draws_count.expect("sampled replay records a draw count"),
+            distinct_count.expect("sampled replay records a distinct count")
+        )
+    };
+    if requested_label.as_deref().is_some_and(|label| {
+        matches!(label, "proof" | "proof_relative_to_image") && label != computed
+    }) {
+        let mut rejected = ClaimOutcome::rejected(vec![Reject::new(
+            "E_CERT_COVERAGE_LABEL",
+            "§12.2",
+            format!("{path}.label"),
+            format!("producer requested {}; the checker-computed outcome is {computed} (fraction {fraction})",requested_label.unwrap()),
+        )]);
+        rejected.elements = out.elements;
+        rejected.draws = out.draws;
+        rejected.distinct = out.distinct;
+        rejected.covered_fraction = out.covered_fraction;
+        rejected.establishes = out.establishes;
+        rejected.image_bindings = out.image_bindings;
+        rejected.token_aliases = out.token_aliases;
+        return Err(rejected);
+    }
+    Ok(out)
+}
+
+#[cfg(test)]
+mod tests {
+    use super::*;
+    use crate::json::parse;
+
+    #[test]
+    fn schema_phase_rejects_missing_and_unknown_fields() {
+        let valid =
+            parse(r#"{"kind":"exhaustive","subject":{},"domain":{},"expected":"oracle"}"#).unwrap();
+        assert!(validate_shape(&valid, "exhaustive", "claim").is_ok());
+        for invalid in [
+            r#"{"kind":"exhaustive","subject":{},"domain":{}}"#,
+            r#"{"kind":"exhaustive","subject":{},"domain":{},"expected":"oracle","extra":0}"#,
+        ] {
+            let outcome =
+                validate_shape(&parse(invalid).unwrap(), "exhaustive", "claim").unwrap_err();
+            assert_eq!(outcome.outcome, "reject");
+            assert!(outcome.errors.iter().all(|e| e.code == "E_CERT_SCHEMA"));
+        }
+    }
+
+    #[test]
+    fn relation_phase_never_invents_an_expected_relation() {
+        for invalid in [
+            r#"{}"#,
+            r#"{"expected":null}"#,
+            r#"{"expected":{"table":0}}"#,
+            r#"{"expected":{"program":"not-a-hash"}}"#,
+        ] {
+            assert!(parse_expected(&parse(invalid).unwrap(), "claim").is_err());
+        }
+        let claim = parse(r#"{"expected":"borrow_frame"}"#).unwrap();
+        assert!(matches!(
+            parse_expected(&claim, "claim"),
+            Ok(Expected::BorrowFrame)
+        ));
+    }
+}

diff --git a/checker/src/object/lexical.rs b/checker/src/object/lexical.rs
new file mode 100644
index 0000000..17c3cfb
--- /dev/null
+++ b/checker/src/object/lexical.rs
@@ -0,0 +1,384 @@
+//! ISA §16.1/§16.2 token spelling and punctuation, before source hashing.
+use super::sec_err;
+type Lexical = Result<(), &'static str>;
+
+#[derive(Clone, Copy, PartialEq)]
+enum Form {
+    Header,
+    Declaration,
+    Registers,
+    Bounds,
+    Instruction,
+}
+
+#[derive(Clone, Copy)]
+enum Atom {
+    Word,
+    Numeric,
+    String,
+    Punctuation,
+    Star,
+    Header,
+}
+
+struct Token<'a> {
+    atom: Atom,
+    text: &'a str,
+    start: usize,
+    end: usize,
+}
+
+pub(super) fn validate(lines: &[&str]) -> Result<(), String> {
+    let mut section = "";
+    for (i, line) in lines.iter().enumerate() {
+        let result = match *line {
+            "" => Ok(()),
+            _ if line.contains('\r') => Err("expected LF line endings"),
+            _ if line.starts_with("section ") => {
+                section = &line["section ".len()..];
+                validate_line(line)
+            }
+            _ => match section {
+                "symbols" | "imports" | "devices" | "layout" | "schedule" | "certificate"
+                | "coverage" => Ok(()),
+                "data" => validate_data(line),
+                _ => validate_line(line),
+            },
+        };
+        result.map_err(|e| sec_err("§16.1", format!("line {}: {e}", i + 1)))?;
+    }
+    Ok(())
+}
+
+fn name(atom: &str) -> bool {
+    let mut chars = atom.bytes();
+    matches!(chars.next(), Some(b'a'..=b'z' | b'A'..=b'Z' | b'_'))
+        && chars.all(|c| c.is_ascii_alphanumeric() || matches!(c, b'_' | b'.'))
+}
+
+fn unsigned(atom: &str) -> Lexical {
+    match crate::rat::is_canonical_uint_str(atom) {
+        true => Ok(()),
+        false => Err("expected a canonical unsigned INT"),
+    }
+}
+
+fn validate_data(line: &str) -> Lexical {
+    let (label, hex) = line.split_once(' ').ok_or("data requires NAME SP HEX")?;
+    let canonical = name(label)
+        && hex.len().is_multiple_of(2)
+        && hex.bytes().all(|c| b"0123456789abcdef".contains(&c));
+    canonical
+        .then_some(())
+        .ok_or("data requires NAME and lowercase even-length HEX")
+}
+
+fn quoted_end(line: &str, start: usize) -> Result<usize, &'static str> {
+    let mut i = start + 1;
+    loop {
+        match line.as_bytes().get(i) {
+            None => return Err("unterminated STRING"),
+            Some(b'"') => return Ok(i + 1),
+            Some(b'\\') => {
+                match line.as_bytes().get(i + 1) {
+                    Some(b'"' | b'\\' | b'n') => (),
+                    _ => return Err("STRING escapes are quote, backslash and n"),
+                }
+                i += 2;
+            }
+            Some(_) => i += 1,
+        }
+    }
+}
+
+fn tokenize(line: &str) -> Result<Vec<Token<'_>>, &'static str> {
+    let mut tokens = vec![];
+    let mut i = 0;
+    while i < line.len() {
+        let start = i;
+        match line.as_bytes()[i] {
+            b' ' => {
+                i += 1;
+                continue;
+            }
+            b'"' => i = quoted_end(line, i)?,
+            c if b"()[]{},:=@^".contains(&c) => i += 1,
+            _ => {
+                i = line.as_bytes()[i..]
+                    .iter()
+                    .position(|c| b" ()[]{},:=@^\"".contains(c))
+                    .map_or(line.len(), |n| i + n);
+            }
+        }
+        tokens.push(Token {
+            atom: atom_kind(&line[start..i])?,
+            text: &line[start..i],
+            start,
+            end: i,
+        });
+    }
+    Ok(tokens)
+}
+
+fn form(tokens: &[Token<'_>]) -> Form {
+    match tokens[0].text {
+        "bennett-object" => Form::Header,
+        "regs" => Form::Registers,
+        "fn" | "oracle" | "action" | "perm_action" | "lproc" | "section" | "^" | "}" => {
+            Form::Declaration
+        }
+        _ => Form::Instruction,
+    }
+}
+
+fn gap(tokens: &[Token<'_>], i: usize, mode: Form, brackets: usize) -> &'static str {
+    let branch_group = tokens[..i - 1].last().is_some_and(|t| t.text == "^");
+    match (
+        mode,
+        tokens[i - 1].text,
+        tokens[i].text,
+        brackets > 0,
+        branch_group,
+    ) {
+        (Form::Registers, "{", "}", _, _) => "  ",
+        (Form::Registers, "{", _, _, _) | (Form::Registers, _, "}", _, _) => " ",
+        (_, "{", _, _, _) | (_, _, "}", _, _) => "",
+        (_, "@" | "^" | ":" | "(" | "[", _, _, _) | (_, _, ":" | ")" | "[" | "]" | ",", _, _) => "",
+        (_, ",", _, true, _) => "",
+        (Form::Header, "=", _, _, _) | (Form::Header, _, "=", _, _) => "",
+        (_, _, "(", _, true) => "",
+        _ => " ",
+    }
+}
+
+fn validate_type(tokens: &[Token<'_>]) -> Lexical {
+    // §16.2 region[INT,INT] is the longest type: six tokens plus its boundary.
+    const MAX_TYPE_TOKENS: usize = 6;
+    let words: Vec<_> = tokens
+        .iter()
+        .take(MAX_TYPE_TOKENS + 1)
+        .map(|t| t.text)
+        .collect();
+    let end = match words.as_slice() {
+        ["region", "[", a, ",", w, "]", ..] => {
+            unsigned(a)?;
+            unsigned(w)?;
+            6
+        }
+        ["qreg", "[", "*", "]", ..] => 4,
+        ["wire" | "reg" | "qreg", "[", n, "]", ..] => {
+            unsigned(n)?;
+            4
+        }
+        ["wire" | "ptr" | "f64" | "token", ..] => 1,
+        [word, ..] if word.starts_with('i') => {
+            unsigned(&word[1..])?;
+            1
+        }
+        _ => return Err("type does not match the §16.2 type grammar"),
+    };
+    match words.get(end) {
+        None | Some(&"," | &")" | &"}" | &"in" | &"mut" | &"token" | &"classical") => Ok(()),
+        _ => Err("unexpected token after type"),
+    }
+}
+
+fn float(atom: &str) -> Lexical {
+    let value = atom
+        .parse::<f64>()
+        .ok()
+        .filter(|v| v.is_finite())
+        .ok_or("invalid or nonfinite FLOAT")?;
+    let rendered = crate::json::ecmascript_number(value);
+    let expected = match (
+        value == 0.0,
+        value.is_sign_negative(),
+        rendered.contains(['.', 'e']),
+    ) {
+        (true, true, _) => "-0.0".into(),
+        (_, _, false) => format!("{rendered}.0"),
+        _ => rendered,
+    };
+    match atom == expected {
+        true => Ok(()),
+        false => Err("noncanonical FLOAT"),
+    }
+}
+
+fn opcode(tokens: &[Token<'_>]) -> usize {
+    let mut i = tokens
+        .iter()
+        .position(|t| t.text == "=")
+        .map_or(0, |i| i + 1);
+    loop {
+        match tokens.get(i).map(|t| t.text) {
+            Some("adj") => i += 1,
+            Some("ctl") => i += 2,
+            _ => return i,
+        }
+    }
+}
+
+fn opcode_widths(word: &str) -> Lexical {
+    word.split('.')
+        .try_for_each(|part| match (name(part), part.strip_prefix('i')) {
+            (false, _) => Err("noncanonical dotted opcode"),
+            (true, Some(width)) if !width.starts_with(|c: char| c.is_ascii_alphabetic()) => {
+                unsigned(width)
+            }
+            _ => Ok(()),
+        })
+}
+
+fn numeric(atom: &str, mode: Form, brackets: usize, angle: bool) -> Lexical {
+    match (mode, brackets, angle) {
+        (Form::Bounds, _, _) | (_, 1.., _) => unsigned(atom),
+        (_, _, true) => float(atom),
+        _ => unsigned(atom.strip_prefix('-').unwrap_or(atom)),
+    }
+}
+
+#[derive(Clone, Copy)]
+enum Number {
+    Integer,
+    Unsigned,
+    Angle,
+}
+
+fn number_kind(op: &str) -> Number {
+    match op {
+        "rx" | "ry" | "rz" => Number::Angle,
+        "qloop" | "qalloc" | "qborrow" | "qregion" | "qreg.new" | "qreg.slice" | "fault" => {
+            Number::Unsigned
+        }
+        _ => Number::Integer,
+    }
+}
+
+fn atom_kind(word: &str) -> Result<Atom, &'static str> {
+    match word.as_bytes()[0] {
+        b'"' => Ok(Atom::String),
+        b'*' if word == "*" => Ok(Atom::Star),
+        b'0'..=b'9' | b'+' | b'-' | b'.' => Ok(Atom::Numeric),
+        c if word.len() == 1 && b"()[]{},:=@^".contains(&c) => Ok(Atom::Punctuation),
+        _ if word == "bennett-object" => Ok(Atom::Header),
+        _ if name(word) => Ok(Atom::Word),
+        _ => Err("invalid NAME or numeric atom"),
+    }
+}
+
+fn header_number(tokens: &[Token<'_>], i: usize) -> Lexical {
+    match tokens.get(i - 2).map(|t| t.text) {
+        Some("ptr_width") => unsigned(tokens[i].text),
+        _ => {
+            let (major, minor) = tokens[i]
+                .text
+                .split_once('.')
+                .ok_or("version requires INT.INT")?;
+            unsigned(major)?;
+            unsigned(minor)
+        }
+    }
+}
+
+fn validate_atom(
+    tokens: &[Token<'_>],
+    i: usize,
+    mode: Form,
+    brackets: usize,
+    kind: Number,
+) -> Lexical {
+    let token = &tokens[i];
+    let previous = tokens[..i].last().map(|t| t.text);
+    match (token.atom, previous, mode) {
+        (_, Some(":"), _) => validate_type(&tokens[i..]),
+        (_, Some("="), Form::Header) => header_number(tokens, i),
+        (Atom::Numeric, _, _) => match kind {
+            Number::Unsigned => unsigned(token.text),
+            Number::Angle => numeric(token.text, mode, brackets, true),
+            Number::Integer => numeric(token.text, mode, brackets, false),
+        },
+        (Atom::Star, Some("["), _) => match tokens[..i - 1].last().map(|t| t.text) {
+            Some("qreg") => Ok(()),
+            _ => Err("* is only a qreg width"),
+        },
+        (Atom::Star, _, _) => Err("* is only a qreg width"),
+        (Atom::Header, _, Form::Header) => Ok(()),
+        (Atom::Header, _, _) => Err("unexpected object header token"),
+        _ => Ok(()),
+    }
+}
+
+struct Context {
+    mode: Form,
+    brackets: usize,
+    op: usize,
+    number: Number,
+}
+
+impl Context {
+    fn accept(&mut self, line: &str, tokens: &[Token<'_>], i: usize) -> Lexical {
+        if i > 0
+            && &line[tokens[i - 1].end..tokens[i].start] != gap(tokens, i, self.mode, self.brackets)
+        {
+            return Err("noncanonical punctuation spacing");
+        }
+        match (tokens[i].text, self.mode) {
+            ("bounds", Form::Registers) => self.mode = Form::Bounds,
+            ("[", _) => self.brackets += 1,
+            ("]", _) => self.brackets = self.brackets.checked_sub(1).ok_or("unmatched ]")?,
+            _ => {
+                let number = match (self.number, i == self.op + 1) {
+                    (Number::Angle, false) => Number::Integer,
+                    (kind, _) => kind,
+                };
+                validate_atom(tokens, i, self.mode, self.brackets, number)?;
+            }
+        }
+        Ok(())
+    }
+}
+
+fn validate_words(line: &str, tokens: &[Token<'_>], mode: Form) -> Lexical {
+    let op = opcode(tokens);
+    let instruction = tokens.get(op).ok_or("missing opcode")?;
+    if mode == Form::Instruction {
+        match instruction.text {
+            "@" => (),
+            word => opcode_widths(word)?,
+        }
+
+        let gap = tokens.get(op + 1).map(|t| t.start - instruction.end);
+        let required_gap = usize::from(instruction.text != "@");
+        if matches!(gap, Some(n) if n != required_gap) || tokens[0].text == "=" {
+            return Err("opcode requires a separate operand and an assignment requires a lhs");
+        }
+    }
+    let mut context = Context {
+        mode,
+        brackets: 0,
+        op,
+        number: number_kind(instruction.text),
+    };
+    for i in 0..tokens.len() {
+        context.accept(line, tokens, i)?;
+    }
+    match context.brackets {
+        0 => Ok(()),
+        _ => Err("unclosed ["),
+    }
+}
+
+fn validate_line(line: &str) -> Lexical {
+    let tokens = tokenize(line)?;
+    let first = tokens.first().ok_or("empty token line")?;
+    let last = tokens.last().ok_or("empty token line")?;
+    if first.start != 0 || last.end != line.len() {
+        return Err("leading or trailing whitespace");
+    }
+    let mode = form(&tokens);
+    if mode == Form::Registers && last.text != "}" {
+        return Err("regs and bounds must close on their declaration line");
+    }
+    validate_words(line, &tokens, mode)
+}

diff --git a/checker/tests/borrow_frames.rs b/checker/tests/borrow_frames.rs
new file mode 100644
index 0000000..70d88c5
--- /dev/null
+++ b/checker/tests/borrow_frames.rs
@@ -0,0 +1,80 @@
+//! ISA-12.1 / ISA-12.2: selected borrow frames remain explicit obligations.
+use crate::common;
+use bennett_cert_checker::{cert::check_certificate, json::Value};
+use common::*;
+
+fn inputs(mut claim: Value) -> bennett_cert_checker::cert::Inputs {
+    // K89 witness: clean c, dirty b, identity on b when c=0.
+    if claim.get("invocation").is_none() {
+        set(
+            &mut claim,
+            "invocation",
+            json(r#"{"args":[],"budget":["0","0","0","0"]}"#),
+        );
+    }
+    standalone(
+        "perm_action @a (t:wire mut) () () () ()\nregs {  } bounds {}\n^entry():\nc = qalloc any 1\nb = qborrow any 1\ncx c b\nqreturn b\nqfree c",
+        r#"{"a":{"abi":"0.9","args":[],"bounds":[],"in":[],"kind":"perm_action","mem":[],"mut":[1],"tier":"q"}}"#,
+        "a", vec![claim],
+    ).0
+}
+
+fn claim() -> Value {
+    json(
+        r#"{"kind":"exhaustive","expected":"borrow_frame",
+    "borrow_frame":{"lifetime":0,"first":"entry:2","last":"entry:2"},
+    "domain":{"bundles":[{"name":"t","width":1,"lo":0,"hi":1}],
+    "borrowed":[{"name":"b","width":1,"lo":0,"hi":1}],"regions":[],
+    "workspace":[{"allocation":"entry:0","offset":0,"width":1,"lo":0,"hi":0}]}}"#,
+    )
+}
+
+#[test]
+fn caq_selected_borrow_frame_products_are_unchecked_until_independently_derived() {
+    for union in [false, true] {
+        let mut c = claim();
+        if union {
+            let product = c.get("domain").unwrap().clone();
+            let mut domain = json("{}");
+            set(&mut domain, "entry_products", Value::Arr(vec![product]));
+            set(&mut c, "domain", domain);
+        }
+        let verdict = check_certificate(&inputs(c));
+        assert!(codes(&verdict).is_empty(), "{verdict:?}");
+        assert_eq!(verdict.overall, "unchecked", "{verdict:?}");
+        let outcome = &verdict.regions[0].claims[0].1;
+        assert_eq!(outcome.outcome, "unchecked", "{verdict:?}");
+        assert!(outcome
+            .unchecked_reason
+            .as_deref()
+            .unwrap()
+            .contains("borrow-frame"));
+        assert!(outcome.elements.is_none());
+        assert!(outcome.covered_fraction.is_none());
+    }
+}
+
+#[test]
+fn caq_malformed_borrow_frame_bindings_reject_before_unsupported_replay() {
+    let base = claim();
+    for field in ["lifetime", "first", "last"] {
+        let mut c = base.clone();
+        let Value::Obj(frame) = c.as_obj().unwrap().get("borrow_frame").unwrap().clone() else {
+            panic!()
+        };
+        let mut frame = frame;
+        frame.remove(field);
+        set(&mut c, "borrow_frame", Value::Obj(frame));
+        let verdict = check_certificate(&inputs(c));
+        assert_eq!(verdict.overall, "rejected", "{field}: {verdict:?}");
+        assert!(codes(&verdict).contains(&"E_CERT_SCHEMA"), "{verdict:?}");
+    }
+    let mut c = base;
+    set(&mut c, "invocation", json(r#"{"args":[],"budget":[]}"#));
+    let verdict = check_certificate(&inputs(c));
+    assert_eq!(verdict.overall, "rejected", "{verdict:?}");
+    assert!(
+        codes(&verdict).contains(&"E_CERT_INVOCATION"),
+        "{verdict:?}"
+    );
+}

+        std::fs::create_dir(&root).unwrap();
+        Self(root)
+    }
+    fn write(&self, name: &str, bytes: &[u8]) -> std::path::PathBuf {
+        let path = self.0.join(name);
+        std::fs::write(&path, bytes).unwrap();
+        path
+    }

+        .arg("--object")

+        .output()
+        .unwrap();
+    assert_eq!(out.status.code(), Some(1));
+    let v = bennett_cert_checker::json::parse(std::str::from_utf8(&out.stdout).unwrap()).unwrap();
+    assert_eq!(v.get("overall").unwrap().as_str(), Some("rejected"));
+    assert!(out.stderr.is_empty());
+    for (path, message) in [
+        (scratch.0.join("absent.bisa"), "cannot read"),
+        (scratch.write("binary.bisa", &[0xff]), "not UTF-8"),
+        (

+            "no certificate section",
+        ),
+    ] {
+        let out = bin().arg("--from-object").arg(path).output().unwrap();
+        assert_eq!(out.status.code(), Some(3));
+        assert!(out.stdout.is_empty());
+        assert!(String::from_utf8(out.stderr).unwrap().contains(message));

+}

--- /dev/null
+++ b/checker/tests/common/pins.rs
@@ -0,0 +1,49 @@
+//! Resolve published test inputs exclusively through this repository's gate pin.
+use std::path::PathBuf;
+
+pub fn isa_spec_dir() -> PathBuf {
+    let manifest = include_str!("../../../gate.toml");
+    let section = manifest
+        .split("[siblings.\"bennett-isa-spec\"]")
+        .nth(1)
+        .expect("gate.toml must pin bennett-isa-spec");
+    let sha = section
+        .lines()
+        .take_while(|l| !l.starts_with('['))
+        .find_map(|l| {
+            l.trim()
+                .strip_prefix("sha = \"")
+                .and_then(|s| s.strip_suffix('"'))
+        })
+        .expect("ISA gate pin must have a SHA");
+    assert_eq!(sha.len(), 40, "ISA gate pin must be a full SHA");
+    let path = PathBuf::from(std::env::var_os("BENNETT_ISA_SPEC").unwrap_or_else(|| {
+        panic!(
+            "BENNETT_ISA_SPEC is required: set it to the detached gate checkout for ISA pin {sha}"
+        )
+    }));
+    let gitfile = std::fs::read_to_string(path.join(".git")).unwrap_or_else(|e| {
+        panic!(
+            "BENNETT_ISA_SPEC={}: ISA pin {sha}: cannot read .git: {e}",
+            path.display()
+        )
+    });
+    let gitdir = gitfile
+        .trim()
+        .strip_prefix("gitdir: ")
+        .expect("BENNETT_ISA_SPEC must identify a detached gate worktree via gitdir");
+    let actual = std::fs::read_to_string(path.join(gitdir).join("HEAD")).unwrap_or_else(|e| {
+        panic!(
+            "BENNETT_ISA_SPEC={}: ISA pin {sha}: cannot read detached HEAD: {e}",
+            path.display()
+        )
+    });
+    assert_eq!(
+        actual.trim(),
+        sha,
+        "BENNETT_ISA_SPEC={}: expected detached ISA pin {sha}; actual HEAD {}",
+        path.display(),
+        actual.trim()
+    );
+    path
+}

diff --git a/checker/tests/fault_records.rs b/checker/tests/fault_records.rs
new file mode 100644
index 0000000..9637c63
--- /dev/null
+++ b/checker/tests/fault_records.rs
@@ -0,0 +1,34 @@
+//! ISA-12.2: rejection records and legal host limits are distinct.
+use bennett_cert_checker::{
+    fault::{HostLimit, Reject, ResolveError},
+    json::parse,
+};
+
+#[test]
+fn rejection_paths_json_and_display_preserve_every_field() {
+    let error = Reject::new("E_CERT_DOMAIN", "§12.2", "domain.width", "width mismatch");
+    let expected = parse(r#"{"code":"E_CERT_DOMAIN","section":"§12.2","path":"regions.root.domain.width","message":"width mismatch"}"#).unwrap();
+    assert_eq!(error.at("regions.root").to_value(), expected);
+    assert_eq!(error.at("").path, "domain.width");
+    assert_eq!(Reject::new("X", "§12.2", "", "m").at("claim").path, "claim");
+    assert_eq!(
+        error.to_string(),
+        "E_CERT_DOMAIN (§12.2) at domain.width: width mismatch"
+    );
+    assert_eq!(error.path, "domain.width");
+    assert_eq!(
+        ResolveError::from(error.clone()),
+        ResolveError::Reject(error)
+    );
+}
+
+#[test]
+fn host_limits_remain_non_rejections_with_the_original_quantity() {
+    let limit = HostLimit {
+        quantity: "domain element count 18446744073709551616".into(),
+    };
+    assert_eq!(
+        ResolveError::from(limit.clone()),
+        ResolveError::HostLimit(limit)
+    );
+}

diff --git a/checker/tests/lexical.rs b/checker/tests/lexical.rs
new file mode 100644
index 0000000..7e7c3de
--- /dev/null
+++ b/checker/tests/lexical.rs
@@ -0,0 +1,42 @@
+//! clause: ISA-16.1, ISA-16.2
+use crate::common;
+use bennett_cert_checker::object::Object;
+use common::*;
+
+fn source() -> String {
+    standalone(
+        "perm_action @a (t:wire mut) (c:wire in) () () ()\nregs {  } bounds {2}\n^entry():\nqloop 2 {\ncx c t\n}",
+        r#"{"a":{"abi":"0.9","args":[],"bounds":[2],"in":[1],"kind":"perm_action","mem":[],"mut":[1],"tier":"q"}}"#,
+        "a", vec![],
+    ).0.object_text
+}
+
+#[test]
+fn eq2_noncanonical_body_tokens_cannot_enter_the_checker() {
+    let valid = source();
+    for (from, to) in [
+        ("qloop 2", "qloop 02"),
+        ("qloop 2", "qloop +2"),
+        ("cx c t", "cx  c t"),
+        ("cx c t", "cx c t "),
+        ("cx c t", " cx c t"),
+        ("cx c t", "cx\tc t"),
+        ("cx c t", "cx c t # comment"),
+        ("regs {  }", "regs { }"),
+        ("wire mut", "wire[01] mut"),
+        ("section functions", "section functions "),
+    ] {
+        let bad = valid.replacen(from, to, 1);
+        assert_ne!(bad, valid);
+        assert!(Object::parse(&bad).is_err(), "accepted {to:?}");
+    }
+}
+
+#[test]
+fn lexical_exceptions_preserve_empty_regs_empty_data_and_quoted_spaces() {
+    let valid = source();
+    Object::parse(&valid).unwrap();
+    Object::parse(&format!("{valid}\nsection data\nempty \n")).unwrap();
+    let quoted = valid.replace("cx c t", "future_op \"a  b\"");
+    Object::parse(&quoted).unwrap();
+}
diff --git a/checker/tests/lexical_differential.rs b/checker/tests/lexical_differential.rs
new file mode 100644
index 0000000..b5df746
--- /dev/null
+++ b/checker/tests/lexical_differential.rs
@@ -0,0 +1,505 @@
+//! Generated ISA §16.1/§16.2 admission differential against the pinned binary.
+use crate::common::*;
+use bennett_cert_checker::{
+    cert::{check_certificate, Inputs},
+    json::{jcs, Value},
+    object::Object,
+};
+use std::{
+    path::PathBuf,
+    process::{Command, Output},
+    sync::atomic::{AtomicUsize, Ordering},
+};
+static NEXT: AtomicUsize = AtomicUsize::new(0);
+
+struct Oracle {
+    dir: PathBuf,
+    binary: PathBuf,
+}
+impl Oracle {
+    fn new() -> Self {
+        let pin = pins::isa_spec_dir();
+        let binary = pin.join("reference-interpreter/target/release/bennett-isa-ref");
+        assert!(
+            binary.is_file(),
+            "build the pinned release interpreter: {}",
+            binary.display()
+        );
+        if let Some(configured) = std::env::var_os("BENNETT_ISA_BINARY") {
+            assert_eq!(
+                std::fs::canonicalize(configured).unwrap(),
+                std::fs::canonicalize(&binary).unwrap(),
+                "BENNETT_ISA_BINARY must be the gate-pinned interpreter"
+            );
+        }
+        let dir = std::env::temp_dir().join(format!(
+            "checker-lexical-{}-{}",
+            std::process::id(),
+            NEXT.fetch_add(1, Ordering::Relaxed)
+        ));
+        std::fs::create_dir(&dir).unwrap();
+        Self { dir, binary }
+    }
+    fn run(&self, command: &str, text: &str) -> Output {
+        let path = self.dir.join("candidate.bisa");
+        std::fs::write(&path, text).unwrap();
+        let out = Command::new("timeout")
+            .arg("5")
+            .arg(&self.binary)
+            .arg(command)
+            .arg(path)
+            .output()
+            .unwrap();
+        assert!(
+            matches!(out.status.code(), Some(0 | 1)),
+            "oracle failed: {out:?}"
+        );
+        out
+    }
+    fn bound_candidate(&self, text: &str) -> String {
+        // The oracle's hash command ignores stale stated hashes. This keeps
+        // accepted whitespace/value changes from being rejected only for §9.2.
+        let hashed = self.run("hash", text);
+        if !hashed.status.success() {
+            return text.into();
+        }
+        let hashes = json(std::str::from_utf8(&hashed.stdout).unwrap());
+        let (prefix, rest) = text.split_once("section symbols\n").unwrap();
+        let (symbols, suffix) = rest.split_once("\n\nsection functions\n").unwrap();
+        let mut symbols = json(symbols);
+        let Value::Obj(entries) = &mut symbols else {
+            panic!()
+        };
+        for entry in entries.values_mut() {
+            let name = entry.get("name").unwrap().as_str().unwrap();
+            let hash = hashes
+                .get("symbols")
+                .unwrap()
+                .get(name)
+                .unwrap()
+                .get("interface_hash")
+                .unwrap()
+                .clone();
+            set(entry, "interface_hash", hash);
+        }
+        format!(
+            "{prefix}section symbols\n{}\n\nsection functions\n{suffix}",
+            encode(&symbols)
+        )
+    }
+}
+impl Drop for Oracle {
+    fn drop(&mut self) {
+        std::fs::remove_dir_all(&self.dir).expect("remove lexical oracle inputs");
+    }
+}
+
+fn identity_claim() -> Value {
+    let mut rows = vec![];
+    for t in 0..2 {
+        for c in 0..2 {
+            let tuple = json(&format!(
+                r#"{{"bundles":["{t}","{c}"],"borrowed":[],"regions":[]}}"#
+            ));
+            let mut row = json("{}");
+            set(&mut row, "before", tuple.clone());
+            set(&mut row, "after", tuple);
+            rows.push(row);
+        }
+    }
+    let mut claim = json(
+        r#"{"kind":"exhaustive","label":"proof","invocation":{"args":[],"budget":["0","0","0","0"]},"domain":{"bundles":[{"name":"t","width":1,"lo":0,"hi":1},{"name":"c","width":1,"lo":0,"hi":1}],"borrowed":[],"regions":[]},"expected":{}}"#,
+    );
+    set(&mut claim, "expected", {
+        let mut e = json("{}");
+        set(&mut e, "table", Value::Arr(rows));
+        e
+    });
+    claim
+}
+
+fn seed(extra: bool) -> Inputs {
+    let root = "perm_action @a (t:wire[1] mut) (c:wire[1] in) () () ()\nregs {  } bounds {2}\n^entry():\nqloop 2 {\ncx c[0] t[0]\n}";
+    let mut functions = root.to_string();
+    let mut sigs = json(
+        r#"{"a":{"abi":"0.9","args":[],"bounds":[2],"in":[1],"kind":"perm_action","mem":[],"mut":[1],"tier":"q"}}"#,
+    );
+    if extra {
+        functions.push_str("\naction @types (w:wire[2] mut) () () (n:i4, p:ptr, f:f64, tk:token) ()\nregs {  } bounds {2}\n^entry():\nd = qalloc any 2\nb = qborrow any 2\nqregion local 1 2\nqloop 2 {\nx d[1]\n}\nqreturn b\nqfree d\nqif w[0] {\nx w[1]\n} {\nx w[1]\n}\nrx 1.0 w[0]\noracle @o (x:wire[4] in) (t:wire[4]) (f:wire[4]) (db:region[0,8] in) ()\nregs { r:reg[4], s:reg[4], zero:reg[4] }\n^entry():\nr = lift.const.i4 -1\ns = lift.const.i4 1\nzero = lift.const.i4 0\nlift.retval r\nfn cc @host (q:qreg[2], dyn:qreg[*], n:i4, p:ptr, f:f64, tk:token) () () () ()\n^entry():\nbr ^next(n)\n^next(value:i4):\nret");
+        set(
+            &mut sigs,
+            "types",
+            json(
+                r#"{"abi":"0.9","args":["i4","ptr","f64","token"],"bounds":[2],"in":[],"kind":"action","mem":[],"mut":[2],"tier":"q"}"#,
+            ),
+        );
+        set(
+            &mut sigs,
+            "o",
+            json(
+                r#"{"abi":"0.9","args":[],"fault":4,"in":[4],"kind":"oracle","mem":[{"A":0,"W":8,"role":"in"}],"tgt":4,"tier":"q"}"#,
+            ),
+        );
+        set(
+            &mut sigs,
+            "host",
+            json(
+                r#"{"abi":"0.9","kind":"cc","params":["qreg[2]","qreg[*]","i4","ptr","f64","token"],"results":[],"tier":"cc"}"#,
+            ),
+        );
+    }
+    let inputs = standalone(&functions, &encode(&sigs), "a", vec![identity_claim()]).0;
+    if extra {
+        let text = format!(
+            "{}\nsection layout\n{}\n",
+            inputs.object_text,
+            encode(&json(
+                r#"{"A_tab":2,"H":6,"S_cells":0,"globals":{},"heap_base":16,"heap_limit_max":32,"interface_regions":{"o":{"db":{"base":4}}},"null_size":4,"ptr_width":32}"#
+            ))
+        );
+        candidate_inputs(&inputs, text)
+    } else {
+        inputs
+    }
+}
+
+fn candidate_inputs(base: &Inputs, text: String) -> Inputs {
+    let mut input = base.clone();
+    input.object_text = text;
+    let Ok(_) = Object::parse(&input.object_text) else {
+        return input;
+    };
+    input.object_text = rebind_object_symbols(&input.object_text);
+    let object = Object::parse(&input.object_text).unwrap();
+    let root = object.symbol("a").unwrap();
+    let hash = root.closure_hash.as_ref().unwrap();
+    let mut cert = json(std::str::from_utf8(&input.cert_bytes).unwrap());
+    let old = cert
+        .get("bindings")
+        .unwrap()
+        .get("closure_hash")
+        .unwrap()
+        .as_str()
+        .unwrap()
+        .to_string();
+    set(
+        &mut cert,
+        "bindings",
+        json(&format!(
+            r#"{{"closure_hash":"{hash}","interface_hash":"{}","object_hash":"{}","reference_program_hash":"{}"}}"#,
+            root.interface_hash, object.object_hash, root.interface_hash
+        )),
+    );
+    let Value::Obj(top) = &mut cert else { panic!() };
+    let Value::Obj(regions) = top.get_mut("regions").unwrap() else {
+        panic!()
+    };
+    let mut region = regions.remove(&old).unwrap();
+    let Value::Obj(r) = &mut region else { panic!() };
+    let Value::Arr(claims) = r.get_mut("claims").unwrap() else {
+        panic!()
+    };
+    set(
+        &mut claims[0],
+        "subject",
+        json(&format!(
+            r#"{{"closure_hash":"{hash}","inherited_controls":0,"variant":"forward"}}"#
+        )),
+    );
+    regions.insert(hash.clone(), region);
+    input.cert_bytes = jcs(&cert).unwrap();
+    input
+}
+
+fn witness_verdict(from: &str, to: &str) -> bennett_cert_checker::cert::Verdict {
+    let oracle = Oracle::new();
+    let base = seed(false);
+    assert!(oracle.run("check", &base.object_text).status.success());
+    assert_eq!(check_certificate(&base).overall, "verified");
+    let text = oracle.bound_candidate(&base.object_text.replacen(from, to, 1));
+    assert!(!oracle.run("check", &text).status.success(), "{to}");
+    check_certificate(&candidate_inputs(&base, text))
+}
+
+#[test]
+fn noncanonical_integer_types_cannot_receive_identity_proofs() {
+    let verdict = witness_verdict("regs {  }", "regs { unused:i04 }");
+    assert_eq!(verdict.overall, "rejected", "{verdict:?}");
+    assert!(
+        verdict
+            .errors
+            .iter()
+            .any(|e| e.code == "E_CERT_OBJECT" && e.section == "§16.1"),
+        "{verdict:?}"
+    );
+}
+
+#[test]
+fn noncanonical_bounds_cannot_receive_identity_proofs() {
+    let verdict = witness_verdict("bounds {2}", "bounds { 2 }");
+    assert_eq!(verdict.overall, "rejected", "{verdict:?}");
+    assert!(
+        verdict
+            .errors
+            .iter()
+            .any(|e| e.code == "E_CERT_OBJECT" && e.section == "§16.1"),
+        "{verdict:?}"
+    );
+}
+
+#[test]
+fn generated_lexical_admission_matches_the_pinned_interpreter() {
+    let oracle = Oracle::new();
+    let base = seed(true);
+    let checked = oracle.run("check", &base.object_text);
+    assert!(
+        checked.status.success(),
+        "canonical seed: {}",
+        String::from_utf8_lossy(&checked.stderr)
+    );
+    assert_eq!(check_certificate(&base).overall, "verified");
+    let (numeric, punctuation) = sites(&base.object_text);
+    let numeric_sites = numeric.len();
+    let punctuation_sites = punctuation.len();
+    let mut failures = vec![];
+    let mut count = 0;
+    let mut accepted = 0;
+    let mut covered = std::collections::BTreeSet::new();
+    for (range, role) in numeric {
+        covered.insert(role);
+        let atom = &base.object_text[range.clone()];
+        for replacement in numeric_spellings(atom) {
+            compare_candidate(
+                &oracle,
+                &base,
+                range.clone(),
+                &replacement,
+                &mut failures,
+                &mut count,
+                &mut accepted,
+            );
+        }
+    }
+    assert_eq!(
+        covered,
+        std::collections::BTreeSet::from([
+            NumericRole::Version,
+            NumericRole::Width,
+            NumericRole::Bound,
+            NumericRole::Literal,
+            NumericRole::Index,
+            NumericRole::Count,
+            NumericRole::Region,
+            NumericRole::Angle,
+        ])
+    );
+    for range in punctuation {
+        for side in [false, true] {
+            for gap in ["", " ", "  ", "\t", "\n"] {
+                let replacement = if side {
+                    format!("{}{gap}", &base.object_text[range.clone()])
+                } else {
+                    format!("{gap}{}", &base.object_text[range.clone()])
+                };
+                let mut changed_range = range.clone();
+                if side {
+                    while base.object_text.as_bytes().get(changed_range.end) == Some(&b' ') {
+                        changed_range.end += 1;
+                    }
+                } else {
+                    while changed_range.start > 0
+                        && base.object_text.as_bytes()[changed_range.start - 1] == b' '
+                    {
+                        changed_range.start -= 1;
+                    }
+                }
+                compare_candidate(
+                    &oracle,
+                    &base,
+                    changed_range,
+                    &replacement,
+                    &mut failures,
+                    &mut count,
+                    &mut accepted,
+                );
+            }
+        }
+    }
+    eprintln!("lexical differential: {numeric_sites} numeric sites; {punctuation_sites} punctuation sites; {count} generated candidates; {accepted} accepted by oracle; {} disagreements", failures.len());
+    assert!(
+        failures.is_empty(),
+        "{} disagreements:\n{}",
+        failures.len(),
+        failures
+            .iter()
+            .take(30)
+            .cloned()
+            .collect::<Vec<_>>()
+            .join("\n")
+    );
+}
+
+#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, PartialEq, Eq, PartialOrd, Ord)]
+enum NumericRole {
+    Version,
+    Width,
+    Bound,
+    Literal,
+    Index,
+    Count,
+    Region,
+    Angle,
+}
+
+fn sites(
+    text: &str,
+) -> (
+    Vec<(std::ops::Range<usize>, NumericRole)>,
+    Vec<std::ops::Range<usize>>,
+) {
+    let mut numbers = vec![];
+    let mut punctuation = vec![];
+    let mut offset = 0;
+    let mut section = "";
+    for line in text.split_inclusive('\n') {
+        if let Some(name) = line.strip_prefix("section ") {
+            section = name.trim_end();
+        }
+        let source = section == "functions" || line.starts_with("bennett-object ");
+        if source {
+            let bytes = line.as_bytes();
+            let mut i = 0;
+            while i < bytes.len() {
+                if b"()[]{},:=@^.*".contains(&bytes[i]) {
+                    punctuation.push(offset + i..offset + i + 1);
+                }
+                if !bytes[i].is_ascii_digit() {
+                    i += 1;
+                    continue;
+                }
+                if i > 0 && bytes[i - 1] == b'f' {
+                    while i < bytes.len() && bytes[i].is_ascii_digit() {
+                        i += 1;
+                    }
+                    continue;
+                }
+                let mut end = i + 1;
+                while end < bytes.len() && bytes[end].is_ascii_digit() {
+                    end += 1;
+                }
+                let start = if i > 0 && bytes[i - 1] == b'-' {
+                    i - 1
+                } else {
+                    i
+                };
+                let role = if line.starts_with("bennett-object ") {
+                    if line[..i].contains("ptr_width=") {
+                        NumericRole::Width
+                    } else {
+                        NumericRole::Version
+                    }
+                } else if i > 0 && bytes[i - 1] == b'i' {
+                    NumericRole::Width
+                } else if line.starts_with("rx ") {
+                    // FLOAT is one atom, not two INTs.
+                    while end < bytes.len() && !bytes[end].is_ascii_whitespace() {
+                        end += 1;
+                    }
+                    // The fractional dot is also a punctuation site.
+                    for j in i..end {
+                        if bytes[j] == b'.' {
+                            punctuation.push(offset + j..offset + j + 1);
+                        }
+                    }
+                    NumericRole::Angle
+                } else if line.starts_with("regs ") && line[..i].contains("bounds") {
+                    NumericRole::Bound
+                } else if line.contains("qloop ")
+                    || line.contains("qalloc ")
+                    || line.contains("qborrow ")
+                {
+                    NumericRole::Count
+                } else if line.starts_with("qregion ") {
+                    NumericRole::Region
+                } else if i > 0 && matches!(bytes[i - 1], b'[' | b',') {
+                    if line.starts_with("regs ") || line.contains(" @") {
+                        NumericRole::Width
+                    } else {
+                        NumericRole::Index
+                    }
+                } else {
+                    NumericRole::Literal
+                };
+                numbers.push((offset + start..offset + end, role));
+                i = end;
+            }
+        }
+        offset += line.len();
+    }
+    (numbers, punctuation)
+}
+
+fn numeric_spellings(atom: &str) -> Vec<String> {
+    let digits = atom.strip_prefix('-').unwrap_or(atom);
+    let leading = if atom.starts_with('-') {
+        format!("-0{digits}")
+    } else {
+        format!("0{digits}")
+    };
+    vec![
+        leading,
+        format!("+{atom}"),
+        format!("-{digits}"),
+        format!("0x{digits}"),
+        format!("{digits}_0"),
+        format!("{atom}.0"),
+        format!(" {atom}"),
+        format!("{atom} "),
+        format!("{}\t{}", &atom[..1], &atom[1..]),
+        digits.split('.').next().unwrap().into(),
+    ]
+}
+
+#[allow(clippy::too_many_arguments)]
+fn compare_candidate(
+    oracle: &Oracle,
+    base: &Inputs,
+    range: std::ops::Range<usize>,
+    replacement: &str,
+    failures: &mut Vec<String>,
+    count: &mut usize,
+    accepted: &mut usize,
+) {
+    let mut text = base.object_text.clone();
+    text.replace_range(range.clone(), replacement);
+    if text == base.object_text {
+        return;
+    }
+    *count += 1;
+    let text = oracle.bound_candidate(&text);
+    let reference = oracle.run("check", &text);
+    let parsed = Object::parse(&text);
+    let admits = reference.status.success();
+    *accepted += usize::from(admits);
+    if parsed.is_ok() != admits {
+        failures.push(format!(
+            "at {range:?} replacement {replacement:?}: checker={:?}, reference={}",
+            parsed.as_ref().map(|_| "accept"),
+            String::from_utf8_lossy(&reference.stderr)
+        ));
+    }
+    if !admits {
+        let verdict = check_certificate(&candidate_inputs(base, text));
+        if verdict.overall == "verified"
+            || verdict
+                .regions
+                .iter()
+                .flat_map(|r| &r.claims)
+                .any(|(_, c)| c.outcome == "proof")
+        {
+            failures.push(format!(
+                "oracle-rejected mutation granted proof: at {range:?} {replacement:?}: {verdict:?}"
+            ));
+        }
+    }
+}

+// clause: ISA-12.1-P7
+#[test]
+fn plausible_wrong_hashes_are_rejected_without_rebinding() {
+    let base = controlled();
+    assert_eq!(check_certificate(&base).overall, "verified");
+    for field in [
+        "object_hash",
+        "interface_hash",
+        "closure_hash",
+        "reference_program_hash",
+        "target_hash",
+        "schedule_hash",
+    ] {
+        let mut cert = json(std::str::from_utf8(&base.cert_bytes).unwrap());
+        let Value::Obj(top) = &mut cert else { panic!() };
+        let bindings = top.get_mut("bindings").unwrap();
+        let original = bindings.get(field).unwrap().as_str().unwrap();
+        let wrong = format!(
+            "{}{}",
+            if original.starts_with('0') { "1" } else { "0" },
+            &original[1..]
+        );
+        set(bindings, field, Value::Str(wrong));
+        let mut changed = base.clone();
+        changed.cert_bytes = jcs(&cert).unwrap();
+        let verdict = check_certificate(&changed);
+        assert_eq!(verdict.overall, "rejected", "{field}: {verdict:?}");
+        assert!(
+            codes(&verdict).contains(&"E_CERT_BINDING"),
+            "{field}: {verdict:?}"
+        );
+    }
+}
+
+// clause: ISA-12.1-P8
+#[test]
+fn every_plausible_output_bit_and_shifted_input_row_is_checked() {
+    let base = controlled();
+    let cert = json(std::str::from_utf8(&base.cert_bytes).unwrap());
+    let root = cert
+        .get("bindings")
+        .unwrap()
+        .get("closure_hash")
+        .unwrap()
+        .as_str()
+        .unwrap();
+    let table_path = vec![
+        Part::Key("regions".into()),
+        Part::Key(root.into()),
+        Part::Key("claims".into()),
+        Part::Index(0),
+        Part::Key("expected".into()),
+        Part::Key("table".into()),
+    ];
+    let mut table_source = cert.clone();
+    let rows = at(&mut table_source, &table_path)
+        .as_arr()
+        .unwrap()
+        .to_vec();
+    assert_eq!(rows.len(), 4); // two independent one-bit interface components
+    for row in 0..rows.len() {
+        for bit in 0..2 {
+            let mut changed = cert.clone();
+            let mut path = table_path.clone();
+            path.extend([
+                Part::Index(row),
+                Part::Key("after".into()),
+                Part::Key("bundles".into()),
+                Part::Index(bit),
+            ]);
+            let value = at(&mut changed, &path);
+            *value = Value::Str(
+                if value.as_str() == Some("0") {
+                    "1"
+                } else {
+                    "0"
+                }
+                .into(),
+            );
+            let mut input = base.clone();
+            input.cert_bytes = jcs(&changed).unwrap();
+            let verdict = check_certificate(&input);
+            assert_eq!(verdict.overall, "rejected", "{row}/{bit}: {verdict:?}");
+            assert!(codes(&verdict).contains(&"E_CERT_REPLAY"), "{verdict:?}");
+        }
+        let mut changed = cert.clone();
+        let mut path = table_path.clone();
+        path.extend([Part::Index(row), Part::Key("before".into())]);
+        *at(&mut changed, &path) = rows[(row + 1) % rows.len()].get("before").unwrap().clone();
+        let mut input = base.clone();
+        input.cert_bytes = jcs(&changed).unwrap();
+        let verdict = check_certificate(&input);
+        assert_eq!(verdict.overall, "rejected", "{row}: {verdict:?}");
+        assert!(codes(&verdict).contains(&"E_CERT_TABLE"), "{verdict:?}");
+    }
+}

new file mode 100644

--- /dev/null
+++ b/checker/tests/pin_environment.rs
@@ -0,0 +1,66 @@
+//! Pin transport must work in an exported checkout with no local gate cache.
+use crate::common::pins;
+use std::path::PathBuf;
+use std::process::Command;
+
+#[test]
+fn selected_path_is_the_supplied_pinned_checkout() {
+    let selected = pins::isa_spec_dir();
+    assert_eq!(
+        selected,
+        PathBuf::from(std::env::var_os("BENNETT_ISA_SPEC").unwrap())
+    );
+}
+
+struct PinFixture(PathBuf);
+impl PinFixture {
+    fn new() -> Self {
+        let root = std::env::temp_dir().join(format!("checker-pin-{}", std::process::id()));
+        std::fs::create_dir(&root).unwrap();
+        std::fs::create_dir(root.join("metadata")).unwrap();
+        std::fs::write(root.join(".git"), "gitdir: metadata\n").unwrap();
+        Self(root)
+    }
+}
+impl Drop for PinFixture {
+    fn drop(&mut self) {
+        std::fs::remove_dir_all(&self.0).expect("remove synthetic pin metadata");
+    }
+}
+
+#[test]
+fn missing_variable_wrong_revision_and_symbolic_head_fail_loud_in_subprocesses() {
+    // Validate the parent pin before testing failures in isolated child processes.
+    let supplied = pins::isa_spec_dir();
+    assert!(supplied.is_dir());
+    let fixture = PinFixture::new();
+    for (head, expected) in [
+        (None, "BENNETT_ISA_SPEC is required"),
+        (
+            Some("0000000000000000000000000000000000000000\n"),
+            "actual HEAD",
+        ),
+        (Some("ref: refs/heads/main\n"), "actual HEAD"),
+    ] {
+        let mut child = Command::new(std::env::current_exe().unwrap());
+        child.args([
+            "--exact",
+            "pin_environment::selected_path_is_the_supplied_pinned_checkout",
+            "--nocapture",
+        ]);
+        match head {
+            None => {
+                child.env_remove("BENNETT_ISA_SPEC");
+            }
+            Some(head) => {
+                std::fs::write(fixture.0.join("metadata/HEAD"), head).unwrap();
+                child.env("BENNETT_ISA_SPEC", &fixture.0);
+            }
+        }
+        let result = child.output().unwrap();
+        let diagnostic = String::from_utf8(result.stderr).unwrap();
+        assert_eq!(result.status.code(), Some(101), "{diagnostic}");
+        assert!(diagnostic.contains("BENNETT_ISA_SPEC"), "{diagnostic}");
+        assert!(diagnostic.contains(expected), "{diagnostic}");
+    }
+}
