diff --git a/docs/checker.md b/docs/checker.md
index d112ddf..2028917 100644
--- a/docs/checker.md
+++ b/docs/checker.md
@@ -427,3 +427,67 @@ Token-free omission derives the unique empty/oracle-singleton partition for
 published older positives; a specification clarification is recorded. Scheduled
 carrier/lifecycle integration remains unfinished, and the value-only coherent
 entry API defers token-bearing replay until it carries identities.
+
+Object parsing checks §16.1 lexical form before hashing function bodies:
+canonical numeric spellings, spacing, LF line endings and comment-free text.
+The empty `regs {  }` and empty-HEX data exceptions retain their specified
+spelling. Metadata JSON and quoted strings keep their own lexical rules.
+
+Schedules containing a recompute cleanup decision remain `unchecked` because
+the checker has not derived that cleanup expansion or its resources. A source
+adjoint's reverse trace cannot certify a different scheduled implementation.
+
+Checker tests require `BENNETT_ISA_SPEC`, which the gate sets to
+`{sibling:bennett-isa-spec}`. The selected checkout must have a detached HEAD
+equal to the `bennett-isa-spec` SHA in `gate.toml`. An unset variable, missing
+checkout, symbolic HEAD or different revision fails with a diagnostic naming
+`BENNETT_ISA_SPEC`; no local-cache path or live sibling is substituted.
+
+After materializing the pin, use the headless environment in
+[quality.md](quality.md) and run this one-line command from the repository root:
+
+```sh
+BENNETT_ISA_SPEC="$PWD/.tmp/gate/cache/bennett-isa-spec@3b1090790d82/bennett-isa-spec" systemd-run --user --scope --quiet timeout 240 cargo test --offline --manifest-path checker/Cargo.toml -j3 -- --test-threads=4
+```
+
+The variable points outside any fresh exported checkout, so the same pin can be
+used without a cache inside that export. See [quality.md](quality.md) for
+measured runtime and coverage limits.
+
+Selected §12.1 borrow-frame relations admit the published §12.2 workspace and
+entry-products vocabulary. They remain **unchecked**: this checker does not
+derive maximal source occurrences, normative entry domains or tensor-factor
+replay, and assigns no element count, coverage or proof. Required frame fields,
+subject/schedule binding and standalone invocation binding are checked before
+this deferral. Domain, occurrence and sampler validity remain named unresolved
+obligations. Ordinary interface relations retain their closed domain schema.
+
+## Canonical source admission differential
+
+Before hashing, the reader checks §16.1 atoms in their §16.2 contexts: integer
+type/opcode widths, version components, unsigned bounds/counts/indices/region
+dimensions, signed integer literals, and canonical finite gate-angle floats.
+Punctuation uses the printed grammar spacing, including the empty-regs and
+empty-HEX exceptions. No host-width cap is added to lexical integer validation.
+
+The default integration test generates mutations at every numeric-atom and
+punctuation position of a canonical multi-function object: 52 numeric sites,
+183 punctuation sites, and 1,933 nonidentity mutation cases. Numeric changes
+include leading zeros, signs, hex, underscores, decimal-looking integer
+spellings and inserted whitespace; punctuation changes remove/add spaces,
+tabs and newlines on both sides. All eight numeric roles must occur in the seed.
+
+Each candidate goes through the gate-pinned release interpreter's black-box
+`hash` and `check` commands and this reader's object parser. The hash command
+repairs stated metadata independently, so a stale §9.2 binding cannot conceal
+an admission mismatch. Every interpreter-rejected candidate is also sent to
+the certificate entry point with bindings rebound if this reader admits it;
+neither overall verification nor a claim proof may result. JSON metadata and
+data HEX use their separate grammars and are excluded from INT mutations.
+
+The test runs the release interpreter under the validated ISA pin and checks
+that any `BENNETT_ISA_BINARY` identifies that same binary. Missing binaries fail
+with a build instruction. The canonical identity control still verifies;
+noncanonical integer declarations and bounds reject with `E_CERT_OBJECT`
+at §16.1. Internal evaluator defense tests inject malformed tokens after a
+valid parse; they do not treat those spellings as legal source objects.
diff --git a/docs/quality.md b/docs/quality.md
new file mode 100644
index 0000000..d6b835b
--- /dev/null
+++ b/docs/quality.md
@@ -0,0 +1,334 @@
+# Checker quality measurement
+
+ISA inputs and the neutral-suite binary share gate pin
+`3b1090790d82a00ac95d30b8da6b42d1d7a9f5d1`. Tests validate the detached
+gate-cache HEAD and never read a live sibling. The pin was materialized and
+its release interpreter built with the pinned gate tool's `verify` command
+against the main checkout and job commit dc5e2e2.
+
+## Reproduction environment
+
+```sh
+unset DISPLAY WAYLAND_DISPLAY DBUS_SESSION_BUS_ADDRESS BROWSER
+export TMPDIR="$PWD/.tmp/quality-checker/tmp"
+export CARGO_TARGET_DIR="$PWD/.tmp/quality-checker/target"
+export BENNETT_ISA_SPEC="$PWD/.tmp/gate/cache/bennett-isa-spec@3b1090790d82/bennett-isa-spec"
+mkdir -p "$TMPDIR"
+free -g
+uptime
+systemd-run --user --scope --quiet timeout 240 /usr/bin/time -p cargo test --offline --manifest-path checker/Cargo.toml -j3 --no-fail-fast -- --test-threads=4
+cargo fmt --manifest-path checker/Cargo.toml -- --check
+```
+
+Builds require at least 6 GB available RAM and one-minute load below 12.
+
+## Default checker tests
+
+| Configuration | Result | Wall time |
+| --- | --- | ---: |
+| Before pin repair | 270 passed, 4 missing-fixture failures | 37.45 s |
+| Updated pin, original binaries | 274 passed, 0 failed, 0 ignored | 79.86 s |
+| Consolidated binary, line-table test profile | 276 passed, 0 failed, 0 ignored | 46.30 s |
+| Quality-floor checkpoint, warm cache | 286 passed, 0 failed, 0 ignored | 28.23 s |
+| Canonical-admission repair | 291 passed, 0 failed, 0 ignored | 26.05 s |
+
+The consolidation run includes its profile rebuild; the final timing uses a warm cache. Every integration case is included in
+`tests/conformance.rs`; no slow tests or exclusions were needed. The two added
+cases cover selected borrow-frame admission as explicit unchecked, malformed
+frame fields and invocation bindings. Complete borrow-frame semantics remain an
+unresolved obligation, with no proof/count/coverage assigned.
+
+The inherited nested-loop, qif-lifetime, sampled-table, signed-literal,
+large-shift, whole-bundle MCX, lexical and recompute-cleanup regressions all pass.
+A recompute schedule retains explicit unchecked obligations.
+
+## Coverage
+
+**Lines: 84.19% (14,587 / 17,326); functions: 82.64%; regions: 85.84%.**
+Measured after canonical-admission repair at the unified pin: 291 passed (277 integration + 14 unit),
+zero failures, without ignoring run failures.
+
+```sh
+systemd-run --user --scope --quiet timeout 300 cargo llvm-cov --offline --manifest-path checker/Cargo.toml -j3 --json --summary-only --output-path .tmp/quality-checker/lexical-coverage.json -- --test-threads=4
+```
+
+This measures Rust checker execution, separately from clause coverage. No
+threshold is imposed. `fault.rs` is now 100% lines: path prefixing, JSON fields,
+Display and both ResolveError conversions are asserted exactly.
+
+CLI line coverage is 86.05%; the extracted replay phases are 92.76%;
+the grammar-based lexical reader is 97.10%.
+
+The five weakest source files have explicit retained work in
+bennett-conformance-ac5:
+
+| File | Lines | Reason / next witness |
+| --- | ---: | --- |
+| `eval/borrow_frames.rs` | 56.41% | Scheduled-context branches and independently derived frame-entry mechanics remain under the full adoption issue; no invented positive proof. |
+| `domain.rs` | 69.02% | Large host-limit/component-shape branches need bounded witnesses that avoid materializing huge domains. |
+| `structural.rs` | 75.08% | Adjoint/library and frame-provenance branches need contract-derived positive compositions. |
+| `eval.rs` | 74.89% | Remaining procedure/memory unsupported branches need bounded independent witnesses. |
+| `target.rs` | 83.10% | Remaining native/fragment descriptor branches need independently derived boundary and malformed-value witnesses. |
+
+## Review and remaining work
+
+Fresh review and council review of verdict changes remain the orchestrator's
+responsibility; green tests are not a CLEAR verdict. Remaining coverage,
+structural, default-audit, clause-map and outside-owned litter work is filed
+under the issues named below.
+
+## Test oracles and clause mapping
+
+Value mutations cover six same-type wrong binding hashes, all eight output bits
+and four shifted input rows of the controlled-action table. Type sweeps still
+visit every field; they no longer hard-code a snapshot's field count. The heap
+store/load witness additionally checks the independently derived payload x and
+zero fault for all sixteen x values, rather than only its verdict/count.
+The test-quality checkpoint passed 269 integration cases; the current count is 277.
+
+```sh
+python3 clauses/clausegraph.py coverage clauses/ISA-0.9.json --tags checker/tests/clause_tags.json
+```
+
+Fifteen mapped tests were confirmed executed in the successful integration run.
+This partial checker-only map reports 671 clauses: 6 strong, 23 weak section-only,
+642 uncovered. It is separate from proof tags and line coverage. The clause graph
+predates the current pinned contract (source hashes differ); the retained tags
+refer to unchanged paragraph text. Updating the graph, K89 tags, Python tests and
+neutral-case aggregation is retained as bennett-conformance-fv9.
+
+## Semantic function phases
+
+`check_replay_inner` was 700 physical lines after borrow-frame admission.
+It now coordinates schema, expected relation, table correspondence, compatible
+program binding, element selection and outcome assignment in 291 lines.
+Direct unit tests cover schema and relation phases; existing mutation,
+control-flow, fixed-image, domain, row-limit and replay integrations cover the
+remaining phases. That phase checkpoint passed 269 integration cases and both new unit tests; the current total is 291.
+Controlled-action CLI verdict bytes, for both verified and unchecked inputs,
+are identical before and after the split.
+
+The remaining oversized functions have one explicit checker owner in
+bennett-conformance-8v5; this structural item is partially implemented and the
+remaining work is filed, without a zero-giants claim.
+
+| File | Function | Physical lines |
+| --- | --- | ---: |
+| `cert.rs` | check_certificate / check_region | 507 / 484 |
+| `domain.rs` | resolve_domain | 408 |
+| `eval/procedures.rs` | run | 342 |
+| `eval.rs` | exec_row / exec_line / check_inverse_pair | 656 / 389 / 362 |
+| `numeric.rs` | check_frame | 330 |
+| `structural.rs` | translation | 328 |
+
+The inventory masks strings/comments and handles array-type semicolons in
+function signatures. Line spans include whitespace; they are structural
+measurements, not semantic complexity claims.
+
+## Fail-fast checks
+
+Three failures were reproduced before their fixes: lifted calls invented zero
+for missing target/fault values, help exited 3, and unknown internal verdict
+states silently mapped to unchecked. Reads now propagate their errors; help
+exits 0; invalid verdict states panic with context. Canonicalization errors
+cannot become an empty hash or equal empty signature/bounds. Sampled replay
+counts assert their established state rather than inventing zero.
+
+The fail-fast checkpoint passed 286 tests; the current count is 291. CLI tests cover verified/rejected/
+unchecked/usage statuses 0/1/2/3, deterministic JSON, missing options, IO,
+non-UTF-8 and missing embedded certificates. Temporary inputs are removed by
+Drop. Remaining optional-operand/component defaults need individual invariant
+tests and are filed as bennett-conformance-hql.
+
+## Structural baseline and push ratchet
+
+`python3 -B scripts/quality_ratchet.py` checks the recorded per-file baseline
+below. One gate check runs its self-tests and the ratchet. Initial missing
+baseline failed first; recording it made the check pass. Self-tests also require
+failure for each worsened metric and new tracked litter, and check raw strings,
+nested comments and array-type signatures.
+
+Scope: checker Rust source (including embedded unit tests) and repository Python
+tooling outside test directories/files. C/IR/object fixtures and tests are not
+implementation complexity. Function spans count physical lines. The cumulative
+over-50/over-100/over-300 counts and maximum length ratchet the length distribution;
+the four noncumulative buckets and function count are descriptive.
+
+Cognitive mass is a reproducible branch-nesting estimate, not a semantic proof:
+Rust control keywords cost 1 plus enclosing control-block depth, and logical
+operators cost 1. Python uses the equivalent AST control nesting plus logical
+operators. Nested Python functions are measured separately. Trivial wrappers
+(single returned call, or a bare Rust call) are counted alongside mass so splits
+cannot hide growth behind wrappers. The gate also rejects increased process-id
+matches and newly tracked litter paths; removing inherited litter is allowed.
+Known outside-owned litter is retained explicitly under bennett-conformance-pem
+and bennett-conformance-bnk.
+
+```sh
+python3 -B scripts/quality_ratchet.py --self-test
+python3 -B scripts/quality_ratchet.py
+git ls-files '*.log' '*.pyc' '*.darc' '*LOCK*'
+rg -n 'bennett-conformance-[a-z0-9]{3}\b|quality-checker|job/|shift [0-9]+' checker/src
+```
+
+The source grep has no matches. The JSON records every file's distribution,
+complexity mass, trivial-wrapper count and process-identifier matches, plus the
+18 inherited tracked litter paths. Ratchet values come only from this repo,
+with no external grade, complexity ceiling or coverage threshold. Baseline
+updates require a reviewed explanation; `--record` is an explicit maintenance
+operation and is never invoked by the gate.

+## Canonical-admission review repair
+
+The two review witnesses were reproduced separately against the saved pre-fix
+reader: both obtained overall verified and an identity-table proof with freshly
+bound hashes. They now reject with E_CERT_OBJECT, section §16.1, and retain the
+canonical verified control.
+
+The generated black-box differential covers 52 numeric-atom sites and 183
+punctuation sites of a canonical multi-function object: 1,933 nonidentity
+mutations, four interpreter-accepted changes, zero disagreements. Before the
+repair, the initial 1,662-case seed produced 755 discrepancies (including
+proof grants). The later seed adds zero-valued literals/dimensions, typed block
+parameters, both structured arms and wildcard punctuation. JSON metadata and
+data HEX retain their separate grammars.
+
+Source checks parse token kinds once and apply the printed punctuation and
+integer/float productions in context. Integer lexical checks have no host-width
+cap. The existing quality baseline is unchanged: lexical cognitive mass remains
+80 and its function-length distribution improves. No ratchet allowance was
+raised to accommodate the repair.
+
+The default checker command passed 291 tests in 26.05 seconds; the successful
+coverage command above also passed all 291 tests. Focused reproduction:
+
+~~~sh
+systemd-run --user --scope --quiet timeout 180 cargo test --offline --manifest-path checker/Cargo.toml -j3 --test conformance lexical_differential:: -- --test-threads=4 --nocapture
+~~~
+
+The test uses the gate-pinned release interpreter (and validates any configured
+BENNETT_ISA_BINARY against that path). It independently refreshes metadata via
+the binary's hash command before check, compares object admission, then
+ensures interpreter-rejected inputs cannot receive overall verification or a
+claim proof. Correcting older -0 region/index positives follows the pinned
+interpreter's §16.1 rejections; canonical positive tests remain, and internal
+MCX defense tests inject malformed tokens after parsing.

+++ b/scripts/quality_ratchet.py
@@ -0,0 +1,223 @@
+#!/usr/bin/env python3
+"""Repository-local structural ratchet; no external thresholds or coverage gate."""
+import argparse
+import ast
+import json
+from pathlib import Path
+import re
+import subprocess
+
+ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]
+BEGIN = "<!-- quality-baseline -->"
+END = "<!-- /quality-baseline -->"
+PROCESS_ID = re.compile(r"\bquality\-checker\b|\bbennett-conformance-[a-z0-9]{3}\b|\b(?:job|wip)/[a-z0-9_-]+|\bshift [0-9]+")
+RUST_TOKEN = re.compile(r'//[^\n]*|/\*[\s\S]*?\*/|(?:br|r)(?P<h>\#*)"[\s\S]*?"(?P=h)|b?"(?:\\.|[^"\\])*"|b?\'(?:\\.|[^\'\\\n])\'')
+CONTROLS = (ast.If, ast.For, ast.AsyncFor, ast.While, ast.ExceptHandler,
+            ast.IfExp, ast.comprehension, ast.match_case)
+
+
+def mask_rust(text):
+    parts, index = [], 0
+    while index < len(text):
+        if text.startswith("/*", index):
+            stop, depth = index + 2, 1
+            while depth and stop < len(text):
+                if text.startswith("/*", stop):
+                    depth += 1
+                    stop += 2
+                elif text.startswith("*/", stop):
+                    depth -= 1
+                    stop += 2
+                else:
+                    stop += 1
+            if depth:
+                raise ValueError("unterminated Rust block comment")
+            parts.append(re.sub(r"[^\n]", " ", text[index:stop]))
+            index = stop
+            continue
+        match = RUST_TOKEN.match(text, index)
+        if match:
+            parts.append(re.sub(r"[^\n]", " ", match.group()))
+            index = match.end()
+        else:
+            parts.append(text[index])
+            index += 1
+    return "".join(parts)
+
+
+def rust_functions(text):
+    clean = mask_rust(text)
+    for match in re.finditer(r"\bfn\s+(\w+)", clean):
+        start = clean.find("{", match.end())
+        if start < 0:
+            continue
+        brackets = 0
+        abstract = False
+        for char in clean[match.end():start]:
+            brackets += (char == "[") - (char == "]")
+            abstract |= char == ";" and brackets == 0
+        if abstract:
+            continue
+        depth, end = 1, start + 1
+        while depth and end < len(clean):
+            depth += (clean[end] == "{") - (clean[end] == "}")
+            end += 1
+        if depth:
+            raise ValueError("unbalanced Rust function " + match.group(1))
+        yield match.group(1), clean.count("\n", 0, match.start()) + 1, clean.count("\n", match.start(), end) + 1, clean[start + 1:end - 1]
+
+
+def rust_complexity(body):
+    stack, pending, mass = [], False, 0
+    for token in re.findall(r"\b(?:if|for|while|loop|match)\b|&&|\|\||[{}]", body):
+        if token == "{":
+            stack.append(pending)
+            pending = False
+        elif token == "}":
+            stack.pop()
+        elif token in ("&&", "||"):
+            mass += 1
+        else:
+            mass += 1 + sum(stack)
+            pending = True
+    return mass
+
+
+def python_complexity(node, depth=0):
+    if isinstance(node, (ast.FunctionDef, ast.AsyncFunctionDef, ast.Lambda)):
+        return 0  # Nested functions are measured independently.
+    control = isinstance(node, CONTROLS)
+    own = (1 + depth) if control else 0
+    if isinstance(node, ast.BoolOp):
+        own += len(node.values) - 1
+    return own + sum(python_complexity(child, depth + control)
+                     for child in ast.iter_child_nodes(node))
+
+
+def file_metrics(path, text):
+    lengths, complexity, wrappers = [], 0, 0
+    if path.suffix == ".rs":
+        for _, _, length, body in rust_functions(text):
+            lengths.append(length)
+            complexity += rust_complexity(body)
+            wrappers += bool(re.fullmatch(r"\s*(?:return\s+)?[\w:.]+!?\([^{};]*\)\??;?\s*", body))
+    else:
+        tree = ast.parse(text, filename=str(path))
+        for node in ast.walk(tree):
+            if isinstance(node, (ast.FunctionDef, ast.AsyncFunctionDef)):
+                lengths.append(node.end_lineno - node.lineno + 1)
+                complexity += sum(python_complexity(child) for child in node.body)
+                wrappers += len(node.body) == 1 and isinstance(node.body[0], ast.Return) and isinstance(node.body[0].value, ast.Call)
+    return {
+        "functions": len(lengths),
+        "length_le_50": sum(n <= 50 for n in lengths),
+        "length_51_100": sum(50 < n <= 100 for n in lengths),
+        "length_101_300": sum(100 < n <= 300 for n in lengths),
+        "length_gt_300": sum(n > 300 for n in lengths),
+        "over_50": sum(n > 50 for n in lengths),
+        "over_100": sum(n > 100 for n in lengths),
+        "max_lines": max(lengths, default=0),
+        "cognitive_mass": complexity,
+        "trivial_wrappers": wrappers,
+        "process_identifiers": len(PROCESS_ID.findall(text)),
+    }
+
+
+def is_litter(name):
+    path = Path(name)
+    return ("__pycache__" in path.parts or path.suffix in (".pyc", ".log", ".darc")
+            or path.name == "LOCK" or ".gate.lock" in path.name
+            or path.name.startswith(("PROGRESS", "LAST-RUN")))
+
+
+def measure():
+    names = subprocess.check_output(["git", "ls-files"], cwd=ROOT, text=True).splitlines()
+    files = {}
+    for name in names:
+        path = Path(name)
+        rust = name.startswith("checker/src/") and path.suffix == ".rs"
+        python = (path.suffix == ".py" and "tests" not in path.parts
+                  and not path.name.startswith(("test_", "check_")))
+        if rust or python:
+            files[name] = file_metrics(path, (ROOT / path).read_text())
+    return {"files": files, "litter": sorted(name for name in names if is_litter(name))}
+
+
+def regressions(baseline, current):
+    errors = ["new tracked litter: " + name for name in
+              sorted(set(current["litter"]) - set(baseline["litter"]))]
+    guarded = ("over_50", "over_100", "length_gt_300", "max_lines",
+               "cognitive_mass", "trivial_wrappers", "process_identifiers")
+    for name, metrics in current["files"].items():
+        previous = baseline["files"].get(name, {})
+        for key in guarded:
+            if metrics[key] > previous.get(key, 0):
+                errors.append(f"{name}: {key} {previous.get(key, 0)} -> {metrics[key]}")
+    return errors
+
+
+def self_test():
+    sample = 'fn array(x: &[u8; 4]) { if x[0] > 0 { call(); } }'
+    metrics = file_metrics(Path("sample.rs"), sample)
+    assert metrics["functions"] == 1 and metrics["cognitive_mass"] == 1
+    raw = 'fn f() { let x = r###"{braces}"###; /* } */ call(); }'
+    assert len(list(rust_functions(raw))) == 1
+    nested = "fn f() { /* outer /* inner */ } ignored */ call(); }"
+    assert len(list(rust_functions(nested))) == 1
+    long = "fn f() {\n" + " call();\n" * 50 + "}"
+    assert file_metrics(Path("long.rs"), long)["over_50"] == 1
+    before = {"files": {"sample.rs": metrics}, "litter": []}
+    for key in ("over_50", "over_100", "length_gt_300", "max_lines",
+                "cognitive_mass", "trivial_wrappers", "process_identifiers"):
+        changed = json.loads(json.dumps(before))
+        changed["files"]["sample.rs"][key] += 1
+        assert regressions(before, changed), key
+    assert regressions(before, {"files": before["files"], "litter": ["probe.log"]})
+    assert not regressions(before, before)
+    py = file_metrics(Path("sample.py"), "def f(x):\n if x:\n  for y in x:\n   call(y)\n")
+    assert py["cognitive_mass"] == 3
+    assert PROCESS_ID.search("quality" + "-checker")
+    print("quality ratchet self-tests passed")
+
+
+def main():
+    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description=__doc__)
+    parser.add_argument("--record", action="store_true")
+    parser.add_argument("--self-test", action="store_true")
+    args = parser.parse_args()
+    if args.self_test:
+        self_test()
+        return
+    current = measure()
+    doc = ROOT / "docs/quality.md"
+    text = doc.read_text()
+    if args.record:
+        fields = list(next(iter(current["files"].values())))
+        rows = [json.dumps(name) + ": " + json.dumps([metrics[k] for k in fields])
+                for name, metrics in sorted(current["files"].items())]
+        encoded = ('{"fields": ' + json.dumps(fields) + ',\n"files": {\n'
+                   + ",\n".join(rows) + '\n},\n"litter": '
+                   + json.dumps(current["litter"], indent=2) + "\n}")
+        payload = BEGIN + "\n```json\n" + encoded + "\n```\n" + END
+        if BEGIN in text:
+            start, stop = text.index(BEGIN), text.index(END) + len(END)
+            text = text[:start] + payload + text[stop:]
+        else:
+            text += "\n" + payload + "\n"
+        doc.write_text(text)
+        print("recorded quality baseline in docs/quality.md")
+        return
+    if BEGIN not in text or END not in text:
+        raise SystemExit("missing quality baseline in docs/quality.md; review and record it")
+    recorded = text.split(BEGIN, 1)[1].split(END, 1)[0].strip()
+    baseline = json.loads(recorded.removeprefix("```json\n").removesuffix("\n```"))
+    baseline["files"] = {name: dict(zip(baseline["fields"], row))
+                         for name, row in baseline["files"].items()}
+    errors = regressions(baseline, current)
+    if errors:
+        raise SystemExit("\n".join(errors))
+    print(f"quality ratchet passed: {len(current['files'])} files; {len(current['litter'])} inherited litter paths")
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    main()
````

## `README.md` (15 lines)

````markdown
# bennett-conformance

The demo ladder as executable gates, plus the tooling to judge any
implementation of the specs. A **consumer only**: nothing depends on it, and it
depends on everything through published contracts and binary edges.

- `ladder/rung-1` ... `ladder/rung-8`: acceptance gates and requirements from North Star section 8. Authoritative status and evidence: each rung’s `RESULTS.md` and `blockers.json`.
- `checker/`: Rust crate `bennett-cert-checker`, certificate checker (ISA spec section 12).
- `harness/`: black-box executor differential harness. Native-versus-compiled comparison with instrumented classifiers remains future work (see `harness/README.md`).
- `clauses/`: clause dependency graph and statement layer of both specs ([README](clauses/README.md)).
- `suite/`: implementation-neutral conformance cases, run against any ISA implementation binary.
- `proofs/`: structured proofs of the invariants the specs lean on (INV-1..INV-6; see `proofs/INDEX.md`).
- legality corpus runner (dialect spec corpus): not written yet.

Gate: `scripts/pre-push` (clean worktree of the pushed commit). Current state and next steps: [bennett/HANDOFF.md](../bennett/HANDOFF.md).
````
