````rust
                    "explicit root claim invocation conflicts with bindings.invocation",
                )]));
            }
        }
        if let Some(sb) = docs.schedule.as_ref().and_then(|s| s.get("bindings")) {
            if sb.get("variant").and_then(Value::as_str) != Some(subject.variant.as_str())
                || sb.get("inherited_controls").and_then(u64_of) != Some(subject.inherited_controls)
            {
                return Err(ClaimOutcome::rejected(vec![rej(
                    "E_CERT_BINDING",
                    "§12.1",
                    format!("{path}.subject"),
                    "root subject variant/controls do not match the scheduled root invocation",
                )]));
            }
        }
    } else if scheduled {
        return Ok(ClaimOutcome::unchecked("nested scheduled invocation: explicit arguments/budget cannot be trusted until every invocation context has been independently resolved (§12.3)"));
    }
    let program = replay_claim::bind_program(&expected, &iface, docs, path)?;
    if expected == Expected::Oracle {
        return Ok(ClaimOutcome::unchecked(
            "expected \"oracle\" compares the realised (§5.2-constructed) operation with F_B; re-deriving that construction requires the §11.1 expansion/step-machine simulation this checker does not yet perform",
        ));
    }
    let (elements, draws_count, distinct_count) =
        replay_claim::select_elements(claim, kind, &domain, inputs, path)?;

    // Scheduled replay compares the realised operation; require an exact
    // realisation so reference replay is the same operation.
    if scheduled {
        if docs.schedule.is_none() {
            return Ok(ClaimOutcome::unchecked(
                "scheduled claim but no schedule document supplied",
            ));
        }
        if docs.expansion_unknown {
            return Ok(ClaimOutcome::unchecked(
                "schedule binds an expansion library this checker does not implement",
            ));
        }
        if let Err(outcome) = crate::realisation::exact_native_subject(&subject, docs, inputs) {
            return Ok(outcome);
        }
    }
    // Replay.
    let c = subject.inherited_controls as usize;
    let mut replayed = 0usize;
    for (i, before) in elements.iter().enumerate() {
        let left = outcome_from_eval(
            eval_subject_tuple_bounded(
                &docs.object,
                &symbol,
                &iface,
                before,
                &invocation,
                c,
                inputs.limits.max_reference_steps,
            ),
            path,
        )?;
        let right: Tuple = match &expected {
            Expected::Table(_) => {
                let rows = table_rows.as_ref().unwrap();
                let index = if kind == "exhaustive" {
                    Some(i)
                } else {
                    domain.index_of(before).to_usize()
                };
                match index.and_then(|i| rows.get(i)) {
                    Some((_, after)) => after.clone(),
                    None => {
                        return Err(ClaimOutcome::rejected(vec![rej(
                            "E_CERT_TABLE",
                            "§12.1",
                            path,
                            "drawn element has no declared-domain table row",
                        )]))
                    }
                }
            }
            Expected::Program(_) => {
                let (psym, piface) = program.as_ref().unwrap();
                outcome_from_eval(
                    eval_subject_tuple_bounded(
                        &docs.object,
                        psym,
                        piface,
                        before,
                        &invocation,
                        c,
                        inputs.limits.max_reference_steps,
                    ),
                    path,
                )?
            }
            _ => unreachable!(),
        };
        replayed += 1;
        if left != right {
            return Err(ClaimOutcome::rejected(vec![Reject::new(
                "E_CERT_REPLAY",
                "§12.1",
                path.to_string(),
                format!(
                    "tuple mismatch at element {i}: before {} replayed {} but expected {}",
                    fmt_tuple(before),
                    fmt_tuple(&left),
                    fmt_tuple(&right)
                ),
            )]));
        }
    }
    let _ = replayed;

    replay_claim::finish_outcome(
        kind,
        &domain,
        &invocation,
        &subject,
        scheduled,
        requested_label,
        draws_count,
        distinct_count,
        path,
    )
}

fn check_inverse_pair(
    claim: &Value,
    claim_index: usize,
    path: &str,
    region: &Value,
    subject: &crate::cert::Subject,
    docs: &LoadedDocs,
    inputs: &Inputs,
    requested_label: Option<String>,
) -> Result<ClaimOutcome, ClaimOutcome> {
    // Find the inverse_pairs entry that carries this claim.
    let pairs = region
        .get("verification")
        .and_then(|v| v.get("inverse_pairs"))
        .and_then(Value::as_arr)
        .map(|a| a.to_vec())
        .unwrap_or_default();
    let entry = pairs
        .iter()
        .find(|p| p.get("claim").and_then(u64_of) == Some(claim_index as u64))
        .ok_or_else(|| {
            ClaimOutcome::rejected(vec![rej(
                "E_CERT_BINDING",
                "§12.3",
                path.to_string(),
                "inverse_pair claim is not carried by any verification.inverse_pairs entry",
            )])
        })?
        .clone();
    let g_hash = entry
        .get("g")
        .and_then(Value::as_str)
        .unwrap_or("")
        .to_string();
    let ginv_hash = entry
        .get("ginv")
        .and_then(Value::as_str)
        .unwrap_or("")
        .to_string();
    if subject.closure_hash != g_hash && subject.closure_hash != ginv_hash {
        return Err(ClaimOutcome::rejected(vec![rej(
            "E_CERT_BINDING",
            "§12.1",
            format!("{path}.subject.closure_hash"),
            "inverse_pair claim subject must be the entry's g or ginv",
        )]));
    }
    if subject.inherited_controls != 0 {
        return Err(ClaimOutcome::rejected(vec![rej(
            "E_CERT_BINDING",
            "§12.1",
            format!("{path}.subject.inherited_controls"),
            "inverse_pair claims quantify over the uncontrolled pair",
        )]));
    }
    let (Some(g), Some(ginv)) = (
        docs.object.symbol_by_closure(&g_hash).cloned(),
        docs.object.symbol_by_closure(&ginv_hash).cloned(),
    ) else {
        return Ok(ClaimOutcome::unchecked(
            "inverse pair oracle is not in the supplied object",
        ));
    };
    let budget = crate::cert::parse_entry_budget(
        entry.get("budget").unwrap_or(&Value::Null),
        &docs.object,
        &format!("{path} (inverse_pairs entry budget)"),
    )
    .map_err(ClaimOutcome::rejected)?;
    if g.kind != "oracle" || ginv.kind != "oracle" || g.signature != ginv.signature {
        return Err(ClaimOutcome::rejected(vec![rej(
            "E_CERT_BINDING",
            "§4.5",
            path,
            "inverse-pair endpoints must be oracles with compatible signatures",
        )]));
    }
    let giface = docs
        .object
        .interface(&g.name)
        .map_err(|e| ClaimOutcome::unchecked(format!("g interface: {e}")))?;
    let domain = match resolve_domain(claim.get("domain").unwrap_or(&Value::Null), &giface, 0) {
        Ok(d) => d,
        Err(ResolveError::Reject(r)) => {
            return Err(ClaimOutcome::rejected(
                vec![r.at(&format!("{path}.domain"))],
            ))
        }
        Err(ResolveError::HostLimit(h)) => return Ok(host_limit_outcome(h)),
    };
    // Bundles/regions must be the full domain of g's in and mem slots.
    {
        let mut errs = Vec::new();
        let mut in_covered: std::collections::HashSet<usize> = Default::default();
        for c in &domain.components {
            match &c.id {
                ComponentId::Bundle { group, slot } => {
                    if group != "in" {
                        errs.push(rej(
                            "E_CERT_DOMAIN",
                            "§12.1",
                            format!("{path}.domain"),
                            format!(
                                "inverse_pair domain bundles cover only g's in slots, not {group}"
                            ),
                        ));
                    } else if c.lo.is_zero() && c.size == (BigUint::one() << c.width) {
                        in_covered.insert(*slot);
                    }
                }
                ComponentId::Borrowed(_) => errs.push(rej(
                    "E_CERT_DOMAIN",
                    "§12.1",
                    format!("{path}.domain"),
                    "inverse_pair domain has no borrowed components",
                )),
                _ => {}
            }
        }
        let in_count = giface.bundles.iter().filter(|b| b.group == "in").count();
        if in_covered.len() != in_count {
            errs.push(rej(
                "E_CERT_DOMAIN",
                "§12.1",
                format!("{path}.domain"),
                "inverse_pair bundles must be the full domain of g's in slots",
            ));
        }
        // Mem fullness: every cell of every region present at full range.
        for (rpos, r) in giface.regions.iter().enumerate() {
            let _ = rpos;
            if r.a >= 64 {
                return Ok(host_limit_outcome(crate::fault::HostLimit {
                    quantity: format!("inverse_pair mem region has 2^{} cells", r.a),
                }));
            }
            let expect = 1u64 << r.a;
            let got = domain
                .components
                .iter()
                .filter(|c| matches!(&c.id, ComponentId::Cell { group, slot, .. } if *group == r.group && *slot == r.slot)
                        && c.lo.is_zero() && c.size == (BigUint::one() << c.width))
                .count() as u64;
            if got != expect {
                errs.push(rej(
                    "E_CERT_DOMAIN",
                    "§12.1",
                    format!("{path}.domain"),
                    "inverse_pair regions must be the full domain of g's mem slots",
                ));
                break;
            }
        }
        if !errs.is_empty() {
            return Err(ClaimOutcome::rejected(errs));
        }
    }
    if domain.n > BigUint::from(inputs.limits.max_elements) {
        return Ok(host_limit_outcome(crate::fault::HostLimit {
            quantity: format!(
                "inverse_pair element count {} (cap {})",
                domain.n, inputs.limits.max_elements
            ),
        }));
    }
    if let Err(h) = domain.check_retained_elements(&domain.n) {
        return Ok(host_limit_outcome(h));
    }
    // Classical arguments: tokens fixed by arg_tokens; others quantified by
    // the domain's args components in listed order.
    let arg_tokens = entry
        .get("arg_tokens")
        .and_then(Value::as_obj)
        .cloned()
        .unwrap_or_default();
    let gfunc = docs.object.function(&g.name).cloned().unwrap();
    let mut token_tuples: Vec<(usize, [BigUint; 4])> = Vec::new();
    let mut non_token_positions: Vec<usize> = Vec::new();
    for (i, ty) in giface.args.iter().enumerate() {
        if ty == "token" {
            let pname = gfunc.groups[4]
                .get(i)
                .map(|p| p.name.clone())
                .unwrap_or_default();
            let raw = arg_tokens.get(&pname).cloned().ok_or_else(|| {
                ClaimOutcome::rejected(vec![rej(
                    "E_CERT_BINDING",
                    "§12.3",
                    path.to_string(),
                    format!("token argument {pname:?} has no arg_tokens tuple in the entry"),
                )])
            })?;
            let tuple = crate::cert::parse_entry_budget(
                &raw,
                &docs.object,
                &format!("{path}.arg_tokens.{pname}"),
            )
            .map_err(ClaimOutcome::rejected)?;
            token_tuples.push((i, tuple));
        } else {
            non_token_positions.push(i);
        }
    }
    let identity_tuples = std::iter::once(budget.clone())
        .chain(token_tuples.iter().map(|(_, tuple)| tuple.clone()))
        .collect::<Vec<_>>();
    let token_aliases = crate::tokens::partition(
        entry.get("token_aliases"),
        &identity_tuples,
        !token_tuples.is_empty(),
        &format!("{path}.inverse_pair.token_aliases"),
    )
    .map_err(ClaimOutcome::rejected)?;
    if domain.arg_widths.len() != non_token_positions.len() {
        return Err(ClaimOutcome::rejected(vec![rej(
            "E_CERT_DOMAIN",
            "§12.2",
            format!("{path}.domain.args"),
            format!(
                "args domain lists {} entries; g has {} non-token classical arguments",
                domain.arg_widths.len(),
                non_token_positions.len()
            ),
        )]));
    }
    for (entry_i, pos) in non_token_positions.iter().enumerate() {
        let ty = &giface.args[*pos];
        let want = if ty == "ptr" {
            docs.object.header.ptr_width
        } else if ty == "f64" {
            64
        } else {
            ty.strip_prefix('i')
                .and_then(|n| n.parse().ok())
                .unwrap_or(0)
        };
        if domain.arg_widths[entry_i] != want {
            return Err(ClaimOutcome::rejected(vec![rej(
                "E_CERT_DOMAIN",
                "§12.2",
                format!("{path}.domain.args[{entry_i}]"),
                format!(
                    "args width {} != type width {want} of {ty}",
                    domain.arg_widths[entry_i]
                ),
            )]));
        }
    }
    let assemble_args = |element: &Tuple| -> Vec<Classical> {
        let mut out: Vec<Classical> = giface
            .args
            .iter()
            .map(|_| Classical::Bits(BigUint::zero()))
            .collect();
        for (i, t) in &token_tuples {
            out[*i] = Classical::Token(t.clone());
        }
        for (k, pos) in non_token_positions.iter().enumerate() {
            out[*pos] = Classical::Bits(element.args.get(k).cloned().unwrap_or_default());
        }
        out
    };
    let in_positions: Vec<usize> = giface
        .bundles
        .iter()
        .enumerate()
        .filter(|(_, b)| b.group == "in")
        .map(|(i, _)| i)
        .collect();
    let elements: Vec<Tuple> = domain.elements().collect();
    for (ei, element) in elements.iter().enumerate() {
        let ins: Vec<BigUint> = in_positions
            .iter()
            .map(|p| element.bundles[*p].clone())
            .collect();
        let cargs = assemble_args(element);
        let run = |sym: &Symbol, ins: &[BigUint]| -> Result<OracleOutcome, ClaimOutcome> {
            outcome_from_eval(
                eval_oracle_bounded(
                    &docs.object,
                    sym,
                    ins,
                    &element.regions,
                    &cargs,
                    &budget,
                    0,
                    inputs.limits.max_reference_steps,
                ),
                path,
            )
        };
        for (first, second, order) in [(&g, &ginv, "ginv(g(x))"), (&ginv, &g, "g(ginv(x))")] {
            let o1 = run(first, &ins)?;
            if !o1.code.is_zero() {
                return Err(ClaimOutcome::rejected(vec![Reject::new(
                    "E_CERT_REPLAY",
                    "§12.1",
                    path.to_string(),
                    format!(
                        "element {ei}: {} faults (code {}) in {order}; the pair must be fault-free",
                        first.name, o1.code
                    ),
                )]));
            }
            let mut ins2 = ins.clone();
            if ins2.is_empty() {
                return Err(ClaimOutcome::rejected(vec![rej(
                    "E_CERT_DOMAIN",
                    "§12.1",
                    path.to_string(),
                    "g has no in slots for the pair value x",
                )]));
            }
            ins2[0] = o1.payload.clone();
            let o2 = run(second, &ins2)?;
            if !o2.code.is_zero() {
                return Err(ClaimOutcome::rejected(vec![Reject::new(
                    "E_CERT_REPLAY",
                    "§12.1",
                    path.to_string(),
                    format!(
                        "element {ei}: {} faults (code {}) in {order}",
                        second.name, o2.code
                    ),
                )]));
            }
            if o2.payload != ins[0] {
                return Err(ClaimOutcome::rejected(vec![Reject::new(
                    "E_CERT_REPLAY",
                    "§12.1",
                    path.to_string(),
                    format!("element {ei}: {order} = {} != x = {}", o2.payload, ins[0]),
                )]));
            }
        }
    }
    let out = ClaimOutcome {
        outcome: "proof".into(),
        token_aliases:Some(token_aliases),
        establishes: format!(
            "for every one of {} elements (full in/mem domain of g, quantified classical args as listed, tokens at the entry tuples) both compositions are fault-free and restore x at budget [{}]",
            domain.n,
            budget.iter().map(BigUint::to_string).collect::<Vec<_>>().join(",")
        ),
        elements: Some(domain.n.to_string()),
        covered_fraction: Some(domain.covered_fraction()),
        ..Default::default()
    };
    if requested_label.as_deref() == Some("proof_relative_to_image") {
        let mut rejected = ClaimOutcome::rejected(vec![rej(
            "E_CERT_COVERAGE_LABEL",
            "§12.2/K85",
            format!("{path}.label"),
            "inverse-pair full-domain proof is not a proof_relative_to_image outcome",
        )]);
        rejected.elements = out.elements;
        rejected.covered_fraction = out.covered_fraction;
        rejected.establishes = out.establishes;
        return Err(rejected);
    }
    Ok(out)
}

#[cfg(test)]
mod fail_fast_tests {
    use super::*;

    #[test]
    fn lifted_calls_cannot_create_missing_target_or_fault_values_from_zero() {
        let object = Object::parse(include_str!(
            "../tests/fixtures/replay-differential/oracle-store-load-heap/object.bisa"
        ))
        .unwrap();
        for missing in ["t", "fr"] {
            let mut work = 100;
            let mut env = Lifted {
                object: &object,
                vals: HashMap::from([
                    ("x".into(), 7u32.into()),
                    ("t".into(), 0u32.into()),
                    ("fr".into(), 0u32.into()),
                ]),
                widths: HashMap::from([("x".into(), 4), ("t".into(), 4), ("fr".into(), 4)]),
                tokens: HashMap::from([(
                    "tk".into(),
                    [9u32.into(), 4u32.into(), 0u32.into(), 0u32.into()],
                )]),
                result_val: 0u32.into(),
                tgt_width: 4,
                depth: 0,
                work: &mut work,
                oracle_name: "o".into(),
                heap_limit: 4u32.into(),
                memory: None,
                locations: HashSet::from(["t".into(), "fr".into()]),
                fault_width: 4,
                region_names: HashMap::new(),
                in_lproc: false,
            };
            env.vals.remove(missing);
            let toks =
                ["lift.oracle_call", "@o", "tk", "(x)", "t", "fr", "()", "()"].map(str::to_string);
            match env.exec_row(&toks, &[], &HashMap::new(), &mut HashMap::new(), &[]) {
                Err(EvalError::Reject(error)) => {
                    assert_eq!(error.code, "E_CERT_OBJECT");
                    assert!(error.message.contains(missing), "{error:?}");
                }
                _ => panic!("missing {missing} was silently initialized by the call"),
            }
        }
    }
}
````

## `checker/src/main.rs` (167 lines)

````rust
//! bennett-check <cert.json> --object <object.bisa> [--target <t.json>]
//! [--schedule <s.json>] [--library <cert.json>]... [--oracle-bin <path>]
//! [--max-elements N] [--max-wires N]
//!
//! Prints one deterministic JCS JSON verdict line to stdout.
//! Exit: 0 verified, 1 rejected, 2 unchecked, 3 usage/IO error.
//! With --from-object the positional argument is the object and its
//! embedded certificate section is checked.

use bennett_cert_checker::cert::{check_certificate, Inputs, Limits};
use std::path::PathBuf;
use std::process::ExitCode;

fn usage(code: u8) -> ExitCode {
    eprintln!(
        "usage: bennett-check <cert.json> --object <object.bisa> [--target <t.json>] [--schedule <s.json>] [--library <cert.json>]... [--oracle-bin <path>] [--max-elements N] [--max-wires N]\n       bennett-check --from-object <object.bisa> [--target <t.json>] [--schedule <s.json>] ..."
    );
    ExitCode::from(code)
}

fn main() -> ExitCode {
    let args: Vec<String> = std::env::args().skip(1).collect();
    let mut positional: Option<String> = None;
    let mut object_path: Option<String> = None;
    let mut target_path: Option<String> = None;
    let mut schedule_path: Option<String> = None;
    let mut libraries: Vec<String> = Vec::new();
    let mut oracle_bin: Option<PathBuf> = None;
    let mut limits = Limits::default();
    let mut from_object = false;
    let mut i = 0;
    while i < args.len() {
        let a = &args[i];
        if matches!(
            a.as_str(),
            "--object"
                | "--target"
                | "--schedule"
                | "--library"
                | "--oracle-bin"
                | "--max-elements"
                | "--max-wires"
        ) && args.get(i + 1).map(|v| v.starts_with("--")).unwrap_or(true)
        {
            return usage(3);
        }
        let next = |i: &mut usize| -> Option<String> {
            *i += 1;
            args.get(*i).cloned()
        };
        match a.as_str() {
            "--object" => object_path = next(&mut i),
            "--target" => target_path = next(&mut i),
            "--schedule" => schedule_path = next(&mut i),
            "--library" => match next(&mut i) {
                Some(p) => libraries.push(p),
                None => return usage(3),
            },
            "--oracle-bin" => oracle_bin = next(&mut i).map(PathBuf::from),
            "--max-elements" => match next(&mut i).and_then(|v| v.parse().ok()) {
                Some(v) => limits.max_elements = v,
                None => return usage(3),
            },
            "--max-wires" => match next(&mut i).and_then(|v| v.parse().ok()) {
                Some(v) => limits.max_wires = v,
                None => return usage(3),
            },
            "--from-object" => from_object = true,
            "--help" | "-h" => {
                println!(
                    "bennett-check: independent Bennett ISA certificate checker (spec section 12)"
                );
                return usage(0);
            }
            _ if a.starts_with("--") => return usage(3),
            _ => {
                if positional.is_some() {
                    return usage(3);
                }
                positional = Some(a.clone());
            }
        }
        i += 1;
    }
    let read = |path: &str| -> Result<Vec<u8>, ExitCode> {
        std::fs::read(path).map_err(|e| {
            eprintln!("bennett-check: cannot read {path}: {e}");
            ExitCode::from(3)
        })
    };
    let read_text = |path: &str| -> Result<String, ExitCode> {
        let b = read(path)?;
        String::from_utf8(b).map_err(|_| {
            eprintln!("bennett-check: {path} is not UTF-8");
            ExitCode::from(3)
        })
    };
    let (cert_bytes, object_text);
    if from_object {
        let Some(path) = positional else {
            return usage(3);
        };
        object_text = match read_text(&path) {
            Ok(t) => t,
            Err(c) => return c,
        };
        // Extract the embedded certificate section's single JCS line.
        let lines: Vec<&str> = object_text.split('\n').collect();
        let mut cert_line: Option<&str> = None;
        for w in lines.windows(2) {
            if w[0] == "section certificate" {
                cert_line = Some(w[1]);
            }
        }
        match cert_line {
            Some(l) => cert_bytes = l.as_bytes().to_vec(),
            None => {
                eprintln!("bennett-check: {path} has no certificate section");
                return ExitCode::from(3);
            }
        }
    } else {
        let (Some(cert_path), Some(obj_path)) = (positional, object_path) else {
            return usage(3);
        };
        cert_bytes = match read(&cert_path) {
            Ok(b) => b,
            Err(c) => return c,
        };
        object_text = match read_text(&obj_path) {
            Ok(t) => t,
            Err(c) => return c,
        };
    }
    let target_bytes = match &target_path {
        Some(p) => match read(p) {
            Ok(b) => Some(b),
            Err(c) => return c,
        },
        None => None,
    };
    let schedule_bytes = match &schedule_path {
        Some(p) => match read(p) {
            Ok(b) => Some(b),
            Err(c) => return c,
        },
        None => None,
    };
    let mut library_bytes = Vec::new();
    for p in &libraries {
        match read(p) {
            Ok(b) => library_bytes.push(b),
            Err(c) => return c,
        }
    }
    let verdict = check_certificate(&Inputs {
        cert_bytes,
        object_text,
        target_bytes,
        schedule_bytes,
        libraries: library_bytes,
        oracle_bin,
        limits,
    });
    println!("{}", String::from_utf8(verdict.to_json_bytes()).unwrap());
    ExitCode::from(verdict.exit_code() as u8)
}
````

````rust
//! ISA §16.1/§16.2 token spelling and punctuation, before source hashing.
use super::sec_err;
type Lexical = Result<(), &'static str>;

#[derive(Clone, Copy, PartialEq)]
enum Form {
    Header,
    Declaration,
    Registers,
    Bounds,
    Instruction,
}

#[derive(Clone, Copy)]
enum Atom {
    Word,
    Numeric,
    String,
    Punctuation,
    Star,
    Header,
}

struct Token<'a> {
    atom: Atom,
    text: &'a str,
    start: usize,
    end: usize,
}

pub(super) fn validate(lines: &[&str]) -> Result<(), String> {
    let mut section = "";
    for (i, line) in lines.iter().enumerate() {
        let result = match *line {
            "" => Ok(()),
            _ if line.contains('\r') => Err("expected LF line endings"),
            _ if line.starts_with("section ") => {
                section = &line["section ".len()..];
                validate_line(line)
            }
            _ => match section {
                "symbols" | "imports" | "devices" | "layout" | "schedule" | "certificate"
                | "coverage" => Ok(()),
                "data" => validate_data(line),
                _ => validate_line(line),
            },
        };
        result.map_err(|e| sec_err("§16.1", format!("line {}: {e}", i + 1)))?;
    }
    Ok(())
}

fn name(atom: &str) -> bool {
    let mut chars = atom.bytes();
    matches!(chars.next(), Some(b'a'..=b'z' | b'A'..=b'Z' | b'_'))
        && chars.all(|c| c.is_ascii_alphanumeric() || matches!(c, b'_' | b'.'))
}

fn unsigned(atom: &str) -> Lexical {
    match crate::rat::is_canonical_uint_str(atom) {
        true => Ok(()),
        false => Err("expected a canonical unsigned INT"),
    }
}

fn validate_data(line: &str) -> Lexical {
    let (label, hex) = line.split_once(' ').ok_or("data requires NAME SP HEX")?;
    let canonical = name(label)
        && hex.len().is_multiple_of(2)
        && hex.bytes().all(|c| b"0123456789abcdef".contains(&c));
    canonical
        .then_some(())
        .ok_or("data requires NAME and lowercase even-length HEX")
}

fn quoted_end(line: &str, start: usize) -> Result<usize, &'static str> {
    let mut i = start + 1;
    loop {
        match line.as_bytes().get(i) {
            None => return Err("unterminated STRING"),
            Some(b'"') => return Ok(i + 1),
            Some(b'\\') => {
                match line.as_bytes().get(i + 1) {
                    Some(b'"' | b'\\' | b'n') => (),
                    _ => return Err("STRING escapes are quote, backslash and n"),
                }
                i += 2;
            }
            Some(_) => i += 1,
        }
    }
}

fn tokenize(line: &str) -> Result<Vec<Token<'_>>, &'static str> {
    let mut tokens = vec![];
    let mut i = 0;
    while i < line.len() {
        let start = i;
        match line.as_bytes()[i] {
            b' ' => {
                i += 1;
                continue;
            }
            b'"' => i = quoted_end(line, i)?,
            c if b"()[]{},:=@^".contains(&c) => i += 1,
            _ => {
                i = line.as_bytes()[i..]
                    .iter()
                    .position(|c| b" ()[]{},:=@^\"".contains(c))
                    .map_or(line.len(), |n| i + n);
            }
        }
        tokens.push(Token {
            atom: atom_kind(&line[start..i])?,
            text: &line[start..i],
            start,
            end: i,
        });
    }
    Ok(tokens)
}

fn form(tokens: &[Token<'_>]) -> Form {
    match tokens[0].text {
        "bennett-object" => Form::Header,
        "regs" => Form::Registers,
        "fn" | "oracle" | "action" | "perm_action" | "lproc" | "section" | "^" | "}" => {
            Form::Declaration
        }
        _ => Form::Instruction,
    }
}

fn gap(tokens: &[Token<'_>], i: usize, mode: Form, brackets: usize) -> &'static str {
    let branch_group = tokens[..i - 1].last().is_some_and(|t| t.text == "^");
    match (
        mode,
        tokens[i - 1].text,
        tokens[i].text,
        brackets > 0,
        branch_group,
    ) {
        (Form::Registers, "{", "}", _, _) => "  ",
        (Form::Registers, "{", _, _, _) | (Form::Registers, _, "}", _, _) => " ",
        (_, "{", _, _, _) | (_, _, "}", _, _) => "",
        (_, "@" | "^" | ":" | "(" | "[", _, _, _) | (_, _, ":" | ")" | "[" | "]" | ",", _, _) => "",
        (_, ",", _, true, _) => "",
        (Form::Header, "=", _, _, _) | (Form::Header, _, "=", _, _) => "",
        (_, _, "(", _, true) => "",
        _ => " ",
    }
}

fn validate_type(tokens: &[Token<'_>]) -> Lexical {
    // §16.2 region[INT,INT] is the longest type: six tokens plus its boundary.
    const MAX_TYPE_TOKENS: usize = 6;
    let words: Vec<_> = tokens
        .iter()
        .take(MAX_TYPE_TOKENS + 1)
        .map(|t| t.text)
        .collect();
    let end = match words.as_slice() {
        ["region", "[", a, ",", w, "]", ..] => {
            unsigned(a)?;
            unsigned(w)?;
            6
        }
        ["qreg", "[", "*", "]", ..] => 4,
        ["wire" | "reg" | "qreg", "[", n, "]", ..] => {
            unsigned(n)?;
            4
        }
        ["wire" | "ptr" | "f64" | "token", ..] => 1,
        [word, ..] if word.starts_with('i') => {
            unsigned(&word[1..])?;
            1
        }
        _ => return Err("type does not match the §16.2 type grammar"),
    };
    match words.get(end) {
        None | Some(&"," | &")" | &"}" | &"in" | &"mut" | &"token" | &"classical") => Ok(()),
        _ => Err("unexpected token after type"),
    }
}

fn float(atom: &str) -> Lexical {
    let value = atom
        .parse::<f64>()
        .ok()
        .filter(|v| v.is_finite())
        .ok_or("invalid or nonfinite FLOAT")?;
    let rendered = crate::json::ecmascript_number(value);
    let expected = match (
        value == 0.0,
        value.is_sign_negative(),
        rendered.contains(['.', 'e']),
    ) {
        (true, true, _) => "-0.0".into(),
        (_, _, false) => format!("{rendered}.0"),
        _ => rendered,
    };
    match atom == expected {
        true => Ok(()),
        false => Err("noncanonical FLOAT"),
    }
}

fn opcode(tokens: &[Token<'_>]) -> usize {
    let mut i = tokens
        .iter()
        .position(|t| t.text == "=")
        .map_or(0, |i| i + 1);
    loop {
        match tokens.get(i).map(|t| t.text) {
            Some("adj") => i += 1,
            Some("ctl") => i += 2,
            _ => return i,
        }
    }
}

fn opcode_widths(word: &str) -> Lexical {
    word.split('.')
        .try_for_each(|part| match (name(part), part.strip_prefix('i')) {
            (false, _) => Err("noncanonical dotted opcode"),
            (true, Some(width)) if !width.starts_with(|c: char| c.is_ascii_alphabetic()) => {
                unsigned(width)
            }
            _ => Ok(()),
        })
}

fn numeric(atom: &str, mode: Form, brackets: usize, angle: bool) -> Lexical {
    match (mode, brackets, angle) {
        (Form::Bounds, _, _) | (_, 1.., _) => unsigned(atom),
        (_, _, true) => float(atom),
        _ => unsigned(atom.strip_prefix('-').unwrap_or(atom)),
    }
}

#[derive(Clone, Copy)]
enum Number {
    Integer,
    Unsigned,
    Angle,
}

fn number_kind(op: &str) -> Number {
    match op {
        "rx" | "ry" | "rz" => Number::Angle,
        "qloop" | "qalloc" | "qborrow" | "qregion" | "qreg.new" | "qreg.slice" | "fault" => {
            Number::Unsigned
        }
        _ => Number::Integer,
    }
}

fn atom_kind(word: &str) -> Result<Atom, &'static str> {
    match word.as_bytes()[0] {
        b'"' => Ok(Atom::String),
        b'*' if word == "*" => Ok(Atom::Star),
        b'0'..=b'9' | b'+' | b'-' | b'.' => Ok(Atom::Numeric),
        c if word.len() == 1 && b"()[]{},:=@^".contains(&c) => Ok(Atom::Punctuation),
        _ if word == "bennett-object" => Ok(Atom::Header),
        _ if name(word) => Ok(Atom::Word),
        _ => Err("invalid NAME or numeric atom"),
    }
}

fn header_number(tokens: &[Token<'_>], i: usize) -> Lexical {
    match tokens.get(i - 2).map(|t| t.text) {
        Some("ptr_width") => unsigned(tokens[i].text),
        _ => {
            let (major, minor) = tokens[i]
                .text
                .split_once('.')
                .ok_or("version requires INT.INT")?;
            unsigned(major)?;
            unsigned(minor)
        }
    }
}

fn validate_atom(
    tokens: &[Token<'_>],
    i: usize,
    mode: Form,
    brackets: usize,
    kind: Number,
) -> Lexical {
    let token = &tokens[i];
    let previous = tokens[..i].last().map(|t| t.text);
    match (token.atom, previous, mode) {
        (_, Some(":"), _) => validate_type(&tokens[i..]),
        (_, Some("="), Form::Header) => header_number(tokens, i),
        (Atom::Numeric, _, _) => match kind {
            Number::Unsigned => unsigned(token.text),
            Number::Angle => numeric(token.text, mode, brackets, true),
            Number::Integer => numeric(token.text, mode, brackets, false),
        },
        (Atom::Star, Some("["), _) => match tokens[..i - 1].last().map(|t| t.text) {
            Some("qreg") => Ok(()),
            _ => Err("* is only a qreg width"),
        },
        (Atom::Star, _, _) => Err("* is only a qreg width"),
        (Atom::Header, _, Form::Header) => Ok(()),
        (Atom::Header, _, _) => Err("unexpected object header token"),
        _ => Ok(()),
    }
}

struct Context {
    mode: Form,
    brackets: usize,
    op: usize,
    number: Number,
}

impl Context {
    fn accept(&mut self, line: &str, tokens: &[Token<'_>], i: usize) -> Lexical {
        if i > 0
            && &line[tokens[i - 1].end..tokens[i].start] != gap(tokens, i, self.mode, self.brackets)
        {
            return Err("noncanonical punctuation spacing");
        }
        match (tokens[i].text, self.mode) {
            ("bounds", Form::Registers) => self.mode = Form::Bounds,
            ("[", _) => self.brackets += 1,
            ("]", _) => self.brackets = self.brackets.checked_sub(1).ok_or("unmatched ]")?,
            _ => {
                let number = match (self.number, i == self.op + 1) {
                    (Number::Angle, false) => Number::Integer,
                    (kind, _) => kind,
                };
                validate_atom(tokens, i, self.mode, self.brackets, number)?;
            }
        }
        Ok(())
    }
}

fn validate_words(line: &str, tokens: &[Token<'_>], mode: Form) -> Lexical {
    let op = opcode(tokens);
    let instruction = tokens.get(op).ok_or("missing opcode")?;
    if mode == Form::Instruction {
        match instruction.text {
            "@" => (),
            word => opcode_widths(word)?,
        }

        let gap = tokens.get(op + 1).map(|t| t.start - instruction.end);
        let required_gap = usize::from(instruction.text != "@");
        if matches!(gap, Some(n) if n != required_gap) || tokens[0].text == "=" {
            return Err("opcode requires a separate operand and an assignment requires a lhs");
        }
    }
    let mut context = Context {
        mode,
        brackets: 0,
        op,
        number: number_kind(instruction.text),
    };
    for i in 0..tokens.len() {
        context.accept(line, tokens, i)?;
    }
    match context.brackets {
        0 => Ok(()),
        _ => Err("unclosed ["),
    }
}

fn validate_line(line: &str) -> Lexical {
    let tokens = tokenize(line)?;
    let first = tokens.first().ok_or("empty token line")?;
    let last = tokens.last().ok_or("empty token line")?;
    if first.start != 0 || last.end != line.len() {
        return Err("leading or trailing whitespace");
    }
    let mode = form(&tokens);
    if mode == Form::Registers && last.text != "}" {
        return Err("regs and bounds must close on their declaration line");
    }
    validate_words(line, &tokens, mode)
}
````
